definition_zh: 恒星的；星体的；极好的；明星级的；星形的
definition_en: relating to stars, or (informally) outstanding and excellent
core_image: 一台望远镜对准一小片天区，屏幕上的光点被拆成温度、质量与年龄三条曲线
scene: 评价一场几乎无懈可击的演出，你说 Her performance was stellar.
sceneCN: 这里 stellar 是引申义「极好的、出色的」（第 3 个义项：由「恒星般明亮」转为对质量的评价）；句意为她的演出极为出色。图中可辨识物件：舞台、聚光灯、评分表、满格星标。

pos.zh: 恒星的；星体的；（口语）极好的；星形的

derivatives.zh: inter- + stellar：星际的；前缀表「在……之间」
non- + stellar：非恒星的；前缀表否定
stella + -ate：星形的；后缀表「具有……形状」
-tor 表装置：仿星器，一种受控核聚变装置；词干取 stellar 的「恒星」义

senses.title: Of or relating to stars
senses.definition: relating to stars in general
senses.definitionCN: 泛指与恒星有关的
senses.example: Stellar astronomy studies how stars are born and die.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星天文学研究恒星如何诞生与死亡。
senses.why: stellar is simply the Latin adjective of stella, so its first duty is to stand beside any noun about stars.
senses.whyCN: stellar 就是 stella 的拉丁形容词，因此它的首要职责是为任何与恒星有关的名词作定语。

senses.title: Of a star's physical nature
senses.titleCN: 恒星自身的物理性质与演化
senses.definition: describing the measurable properties of a star, such as its mass, temperature or evolutionary stage
senses.definitionCN: 描述恒星可测的性质，如质量、温度或演化阶段
senses.example: Stellar mass decides how a star will end.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星质量决定一颗恒星将如何终结。
senses.why: once astronomers could measure stars, the adjective attached itself to the quantities that define them.
senses.whyCN: 当天文学家能测量恒星之后，这个形容词就附着在定义恒星的那些量上。

senses.title: Outstanding, excellent
senses.definition: extremely good; excellent, especially in performance or quality
senses.definitionCN: 极好的；尤指表现或质量出色
senses.example: Her performance was stellar.
senses.exampleCN: 她的演出极为出色。
senses.why: the praise sense is figurative: something stellar shines like a star compared with everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 这层赞美义是比喻：某物与周围相比，亮得像一颗星。

senses.title: Of a star-studded cast
senses.titleCN: 明星云集的；由明星组成的
senses.definition: featuring famous performers; used of a cast or lineup
senses.definitionCN: 由著名表演者组成的；用于阵容
senses.example: The film drew a stellar cast of stage actors.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片召集了一批明星级的舞台演员。
senses.why: the sky image slides from real stars to stage stars, and the adjective follows the same path as the noun star.
senses.whyCN: 天空的意象从真星滑向舞台明星，形容词与名词 star 走的是同一条路。

senses.title: Star-shaped
senses.definition: shaped like a star, with radiating points, as some hairs or crystals
senses.definitionCN: 形状像星、带放射状尖角的，如某些毛发或晶体
senses.example: The leaf surface is covered with stellar hairs.
senses.exampleCN: 叶面覆盖着星状毛。
senses.why: this sense keeps the oldest visual meaning of stella, the drawn or natural shape with rays.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了 stella 最古老的视觉含义：带放射线的画成或天然形状。

senses.title: Of a star's emitted material
senses.titleCN: 恒星喷出的物质与辐射
senses.definition: describing matter or radiation flowing out from a star, as in stellar wind
senses.definitionCN: 描述从恒星流出的物质或辐射，如星风
senses.example: The stellar wind strips the planet of its atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 星风把行星的大气剥走。
senses.why: wind and radiation are properties of the star in action, so the adjective marks them as coming from the star rather than from elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 风与辐射是恒星在活动时的表现，因此这个形容词标明它们来自恒星而非别处。

senses.title: Of a star-forming region
senses.definition: describing the clouds and regions where new stars are forming
senses.definitionCN: 描述正在形成新恒星的云气与区域
senses.example: Dust hides the young stars inside the stellar nursery.
senses.exampleCN: 尘埃遮住了恒星育婴室里年轻的恒星。
senses.why: a nursery is where new lives begin, so astronomers borrowed the domestic word and kept the adjective to mark what is being born.
senses.whyCN: 育婴室是新生命开始之处，天文学家借来这个日常词，并保留形容词以标明诞生的是恒星。

senses.title: Radiant, shining (literary)
senses.definition: shining or radiant in a literary description, often of light or a smile
senses.definitionCN: 文学描写中光辉四射的，常用于光或笑容
senses.example: A stellar glow filled the hall as the lamps were lit.
senses.exampleCN: 灯点亮时，一片星光般的光辉充满大厅。
senses.why: the literal shine and the figurative praise meet here: what shines is praised for shining.
senses.whyCN: 字面的「发光」与比喻的「赞美」在此会合：发光者因发光而被称赞。

intro.en: Stellar is Latin stellaris 'of stars', built on stella 'star' with the adjective suffix -aris. It entered English as an astronomical adjective and later acquired a colloquial sense of excellence. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stellar 是拉丁 stellaris「恒星的」，由 stella「星」加形容词后缀 -aris 构成。它作为天文学形容词进入英语，后来又获得「出色」的口语义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stella 'star' is the Latin noun, a cognate of English star and Greek aster rather than their source; all go back to a reconstructed Indo-European root.
items.cn: stella 是拉丁语「星」，与英语 star、希腊 aster 属同源，而非它们的来源；三者都出自一个印欧重构词根。

items.en: Stella plus -aris produced stellaris 'of stars', the ordinary adjective used with such nouns as stellarum motus 'motion of the stars'.
items.cn: stella 加 -aris 构成 stellaris「恒星的」，是与「星的运动」等短语搭配的普通形容词。

items.en: The adjective is generally believed to have entered English astronomical writing in the seventeenth century, alongside other Latin scientific adjectives.
items.cn: 一般认为，这个形容词在 17 世纪随其他拉丁科学形容词一起进入英语天文写作。

items.en: The informal sense 'outstanding' is nineteenth-century and later; it extends the literal shine of a star to any performance that seems to outshine its surroundings.
items.cn: 「出色」的口语义出现于 19 世纪及以后；它把恒星字面的光亮扩展到任何看似盖过周围的表现。

items.en: The star-shaped sense is also nineteenth-century, when descriptive botany borrowed stellar for radiating hairs and crystals.
items.cn: 星形义同样出现于 19 世纪，当时描述性植物学借 stellar 指放射状的毛与晶体。

items.en: Root uncertainty: the Indo-European form behind stella is a reconstruction. First-date uncertainty only: the earliest use of the praise sense is not exactly dated and is usually placed in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 词根存疑：stella 背后的印欧形式属重构。仅首见年代存疑：赞美义的最早用例没有确切年代，通常定在 19 世纪。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives and nouns of the same star stock that are easily confused; group two holds the ordinary words that compete with the praise sense.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「星」词干、容易混淆的形容词与名词；第二组是与「出色」义竞争的普通词。

entries.definition: From Latin stellatus 'set with stars', it means shaped like a star and is used in botany; it does not mean 'of stars'.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 stellatus「布满星」，意为星形的，用于植物学；它不表示「恒星的」。

entries.definition: Inter- 'between' plus stellar: it names the space or matter between stars, not a quality of a single star.
entries.definitionCN: inter-「在……之间」加 stellar：指恒星之间的空间或物质，而非单颗恒星的性质。

entries.definition: The noun names the body itself; stellar is only the adjective, so a sentence needs star where a thing is meant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指天体本身；stellar 只是形容词，指「东西」时须用 star。

entries.definition: The neutral, everyday word for very good; stellar is informal and adds the image of shining.
entries.definitionCN: 中性、日常的「很好」；stellar 属口语并多了「发光」的意象。

entries.definition: Praise for being clearly above others; it stresses comparison, while stellar stresses brightness.
entries.definitionCN: 赞扬明显高于其余；它强调比较，而 stellar 强调光亮。

entries.definition: From Greek astron 'star'; it belongs to astrology and esoteric writing, where stellar belongs to physics and praise.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 astron「星」；多用于占星与秘学文本，而 stellar 用于物理与赞美。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: stella 'star' + -ar 'of': of a star.
normal.cn: stella「星」+ -ar「……的」：星的。

normal.en: Physics collocations: stellar mass, stellar wind, stellar evolution.
normal.cn: 物理搭配：恒星质量、星风、恒星演化。

normal.en: Praise collocations: a stellar performance, a stellar cast.
normal.cn: 赞美搭配：出色的演出、明星阵容。

normal.en: The same stock gives constellation and interstellar.
normal.cn: 同一词干还给出 constellation 与 interstellar。

normal.en: Stellate means star-shaped, not of stars.
normal.cn: stellate 意为星形，不是「恒星的」。

abstract.en: Picture a single lamp so bright that everything else in the room looks grey.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯亮到房间里其他东西都显得灰暗。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard where one name is printed larger than the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记分牌，其中一个名字印得比别的大。

abstract.en: Picture a crystal cut into rays around a centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一块晶体围绕中心被切成放射状。

examples.en: Stellar evolution depends on how much gas the cloud contains.
examples.cn: 恒星演化取决于云气含有多少物质。

examples.en: The orchestra gave a stellar performance on opening night.
examples.cn: 乐团在首演夜献上极为出色的演出。

examples.en: Stellar parallax is the tiny shift seen as the earth moves.
examples.cn: 恒星视差是地球移动时看到的微小位移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「stellar」听着像「是他了」——全场最亮的那颗星「是他了」 → 恒星的；出色的

root: 拉丁 stella「星」+ -aris「……的」→ stellaris「恒星的」；stella 与英语 star、希腊 aster 同源，印欧词根属重构形式；「出色」义一般认为始于 19 世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: the literal 'of a star' is applied to a star's physics, its wind, its nursery and its shape, and then the same brightness is borrowed for a great performance, a famous cast and even a literary glow.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个形容词展开：字面的「恒星的」依次用于恒星的物理、星风、育婴区与形状；随后同样的「亮」被借去形容出色的演出、明星阵容，乃至文学描写中的光辉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lamp so bright that the rest of the room falls into grey.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯亮到房间里其余一切都落进灰色。

branches.en: THE PLAIN ADJECTIVE: it belongs to any noun about stars.
branches.cn: 普通定语：可与任何关于恒星的名词搭配。

branches.en: THE STAR AT WORK: what it is made of, what it blows out, where it is born.
branches.cn: 工作中的恒星：由什么构成、吹出什么、在哪里诞生。

branches.en: THE DRAWN SHAPE: rays around a centre, not a body in space.
branches.cn: 画出的形状：围绕中心的射线，而非天上的天体。

branches.en: PRAISE: a performance that outshines its surroundings.
branches.cn: 赞美：盖过周围的表现。

branches.en: BORROWED BRIGHTNESS: famous faces and literary glow.
branches.cn: 借来的光：明星面孔与文学中的光辉。

intro.en: Stellar is a Latin root plus adjective suffix; the root also builds several nouns and verbs through the same stella.
intro.cn: stellar 是拉丁词根加形容词后缀；这个词根还经同一个 stella 构成若干名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin stella gives stellar, stellate, constellation and stellify; Greek aster gives astral and asteroid, a parallel family rather than the same one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stella 给出 stellar、stellate、constellation、stellify；希腊 aster 给出 astral 与 asteroid，是并行词族而非同一族。

items.example: Stella is a cognate, not the source, of English star.
items.exampleCN: stella 是英语 star 的同源词，不是来源。

items.example: Stellaris is stella plus this suffix.
items.exampleCN: stellaris 就是 stella 加这个后缀。

items.example: The adjective entered English through scientific Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经科学拉丁语进入英语。

items.example: Botany uses it for radiating hairs.
items.exampleCN: 植物学用它指放射状毛。

items.example: The noun names a group, not a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指一群，而非一种性质。

items.example: It names the space between stars.

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀反转了形容词。

items.example: Rare, but built on the same root.
The device is named for the stellar plasma it mimics.
items.exampleCN: 这种装置因模仿恒星等离子体而得名。

definition_zh: 依赖；依靠；取决于；信赖；指望
definition_en: to rely on something for support or survival, to be decided by a condition, or to trust a person
core_image: 一只吊篮用一根绳子挂在梁上，篮里的重量一增，绳子就绷紧，梁也跟着微微下沉
scene: 果园主人蹲在干裂的土上，抬头看天，又翻看手机里的降雨预报。 The size of the crop may depend on rain in the next three weeks.
sceneCN: 这里指收成多少由某个条件决定（第 2 个义项：结果取决于某一因素）；句意为收成的大小可能取决于未来三周的降雨。图中可辨识物件：干裂的土、果树、降雨预报、水桶。

pos.zh: 依赖；依靠（不及物动词短语加介词，后接所依靠的人或物）
取决于；视……而定（后接条件、变量或情况）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示状态的名词尾构成，义为「依赖；依靠」
由动词加形容词尾构成，义为「依赖的；受扶养者」
由动词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可靠的」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「独立的」
由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「依附关系；属地」

senses.title: Rely on for survival
senses.definition: to need something in order to live or to keep operating
senses.definitionCN: 为了生存或继续运转而需要某物
senses.example: The village must depend on the spring for drinking water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄必须依靠那眼泉水取饮用水。
senses.why: The core verb meant to hang from something; what hangs from a support cannot stand without it.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词本义是「从某物上悬垂」；挂在支撑物上的东西，离开它便立不住。

senses.title: Be decided by a condition
senses.definition: to have one's outcome fixed by a stated factor
senses.definitionCN: 结果由某一明确因素决定
senses.example: The harvest can depend on two weeks of dry weather in June.
senses.exampleCN: 收成可能取决于六月里连续两周的干燥天气。
senses.why: What hangs from a support has its place fixed by that support, so a harvest hangs from rain.
senses.whyCN: 挂在支撑上的东西，位置由支撑决定，因此收成挂在雨上。

senses.title: Trust a person
senses.definition: to place one's confidence in someone's reliability
senses.definitionCN: 把信心放在某人的可靠之上
senses.example: Readers should depend on the handbook only after checking its sources.
senses.exampleCN: 读者只有在核对手册的来源之后，才应信赖它。
senses.why: Trust is hanging one's confidence on another person's reliability.
senses.whyCN: 信赖，是把信心挂在另一个人的可靠上。

senses.title: Rely economically
senses.definition: to have one's income or livelihood tied to one source
senses.definitionCN: 收入或生计系于单一来源
senses.example: The island may depend on a single crop for most of its income.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛可能依赖单一作物获取大部分收入。
senses.why: A single crop is a single rope holding an island's income.
senses.whyCN: 单一作物就是吊住整岛收入的一根绳子。

senses.title: Rely on a habitat
senses.definition: to survive only in a particular environment
senses.definitionCN: 只能在特定环境中存活
senses.example: The beetle can depend on one kind of rotting log.
senses.exampleCN: 这种甲虫可能只依赖一种腐木生存。
senses.why: A beetle hangs from one kind of log, and nowhere else holds it up.
senses.whyCN: 甲虫挂在一种腐木上，别处托不住它。

senses.title: Vary with a variable
senses.definition: to change in value as another measured quantity changes
senses.definitionCN: 数值随另一测量量的变化而变化
senses.example: The measured rate should depend on temperature and pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 测得的速率应随温度与压力而变化。
senses.why: A measured rate hangs from the conditions that set it.
senses.whyCN: 测得的速率挂在决定它的那些条件上。

senses.title: Be conditional in planning
senses.definition: to remain undecided until a future condition is known
senses.definitionCN: 在未来的条件明确之前不作定论
senses.example: The launch may depend on the wind at the pad.
senses.exampleCN: 发射可能要看发射台上的风况而定。
senses.why: A launch hangs from the wind at the pad, a condition not yet known.
senses.whyCN: 发射挂在发射台的风况上，而那条件尚未可知。

senses.title: Rely on a substance
senses.definition: to be unable to function without a drug or a habit
senses.definitionCN: 离开某种药物或习惯便无法正常运转
senses.example: Patients should not depend on sleeping pills for more than a month.
senses.exampleCN: 患者不应连续一个多月依赖安眠药。
senses.why: A sleeper hangs from a pill when the body can no longer hold the night alone.
senses.whyCN: 当身体无法独自撑过夜晚，睡眠就挂在药片上。

senses.title: Count on someone to act
senses.definition: to expect a person to perform a task one needs done
senses.definitionCN: 期待某人去完成自己需要完成的事
senses.example: The committee must depend on volunteers to staff the doors.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会必须依靠志愿者来守门。
senses.why: A committee hangs from volunteers when no one is paid to stand at the door.
senses.whyCN: 没有人领薪守门时，委员会就挂在志愿者身上。

intro.en: The phrase centres on a Latin verb meaning to hang down from something. Every sense keeps the picture of a weight suspended: what hangs needs the thing it hangs from, and its position is fixed by that support.
intro.cn: 这个短语的核心是拉丁语中表示「从某物下垂」的动词。每个义项都保留「重物悬垂」的画面：挂着的东西需要所挂之处，它的位置也由那个支撑决定。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang, to weigh, and it stands behind pendant, suspend and pendulum.
items.cn: 这个词意为「悬挂、称重」，吊坠、悬停与摆锤诸词都由它而来。

items.en: De- 'down from' plus pendere produced dependere, to hang from something, to be attached to it.
items.cn: 表示「自下」的前缀加「悬挂」，构成「挂在某物上、附着于它」的动词。

items.en: Old French carried the verb with the sense of being subject to another's will.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入「受他人意志支配」的意思。

items.en: English took it first for being sustained by something, then for being decided by a condition.
items.cn: 英语最初用它表示「由某物支撑」，随后表示「由某条件决定」。

items.en: The frame with on fixed in the following centuries for support, condition and trust alike. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 与介词搭配的框架在此后几个世纪固定下来，兼指支撑、条件与信任。最早书证年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin hanging verb; the second group holds other verbs of relying or being decided.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁「悬挂」动词；第二组是其他表示「依靠」或「由……决定」的动词。

entries.definition: It describes a person or thing that relies on another; the phrase states the reliance as an action.
entries.definitionCN: 它形容依赖他人的人或物；短语则把这种依赖说成一个动作。

entries.definition: The noun names the state of relying; it cannot take the specific condition as its object.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指「依赖的状态」，不能像短语那样带出具体的条件。

entries.definition: It says that nothing hangs from another support, the exact reverse of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 表示不挂在别的支撑上，正是本短语的反面。

entries.definition: From the same hanging verb, it means awaiting a decision; it shares the image but not the reliance.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「悬挂」动词，意为「待决的」；共享意象，却不含「依靠」。

entries.definition: It stresses confidence in the support, and is common for people and services rather than for equations.
entries.definitionCN: 强调对支撑的信心，多用于人与服务，少用于方程式。

entries.definition: It adds the note of expecting a person to act; the phrase can mean this but does not stress expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 多一层「期待某人行动」的意思；本短语可含此义，但不强调期待。

entries.definition: A vivid phrase for an outcome that turns on a single factor, as a door turns on a hinge.
entries.definitionCN: 形象地表示结果系于单一因素，如门绕铰链转动。

entries.definition: A formal phrase for a result that follows only if a condition holds; it is limited to the conditional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 正式表示「只有在某条件成立时结果才成立」，只覆盖条件义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the hanging basket, the dry field, the sleeping pill and the volunteer at the door.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用吊篮、干裂的田、安眠药与守门的志愿者四个场景。

normal.en: A basket hung from a beam: add weight and the rope tightens and the beam dips.
normal.cn: 篮子挂在梁上：加重一点，绳就绷紧，梁也下沉。

normal.en: A cracked field, a rain forecast, and a farmer doing arithmetic in his head.
normal.cn: 干裂的田、一份降雨预报，农夫在心里算账。

normal.en: One beetle, one kind of rotting log, nowhere else to go.
normal.cn: 一种甲虫，一种腐木，别处无处可去。

normal.en: A pill that must be taken or the night does not end.
normal.cn: 一片必须吃的药，不吃夜就到不了头。

normal.en: A volunteer standing at the door because no one is paid to.
normal.cn: 志愿者守在门口，因为没有人是领薪的。

abstract.en: To depend is to have one's position fixed by something outside oneself.
abstract.cn: 依赖，就是自己的位置由身外之物决定。

abstract.en: Every support is also a limit: what holds you up decides how far you can move.
abstract.cn: 每个支撑同时是限制：托住你的东西，也决定你能走多远。

abstract.en: The same hanging image covers water, weather, trust and truth, because all of them hold something up.
abstract.cn: 同一个「悬挂」意象覆盖水、天气、信任与真值，因为它们都托着某物。

examples.en: Coastal cities may depend on desalination if the rivers keep shrinking.
examples.cn: 若河流继续萎缩，沿海城市可能依赖海水淡化。

examples.en: The final cost should depend on how much material is reused.
examples.cn: 最终成本应取决于有多少材料被再利用。

examples.en: A referee must depend on the linesman's view of the touchline.
examples.cn: 裁判必须依靠边裁对边线的判断。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪彭德 昂」：把「悬挂」记成吊篮挂在梁上——绳在梁上，篮才不落地，这就是依赖

root: 核心动词出自拉丁语，由表示「自下」的前缀加表示「悬挂、称重」的动词构成，本义是「挂在某物上」，引申为「依靠、由……决定、信赖」。介词为本族常用词。整条短语保留「悬挂者离不开支撑」的意象。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses hang from something: water, a condition, a person's reliability, a single export, a habitat, a measured variable, a future wind, a drug, and a volunteer.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项各自挂在一处：水、条件、某人的可靠、单一出口、栖息地、测量变量、未来的风、药物与志愿者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket hung from a beam, its rope tightening as weight is added, the beam bending under the pull.
core.cn: 核心意象：篮子挂在梁上，加重时绳子绷紧，梁也被拉得微弯。

branches.en: THE LIVING SUPPORT: a spring and a single crop keep a community alive.
branches.cn: 活命的支撑：泉水与单一作物，维系着一个社区的生存。

branches.en: THE HABITAT: one kind of rotting log is the only thing that holds a beetle up.
branches.cn: 栖息地：一种腐木，是唯一托住这种甲虫的东西。

branches.en: THE MOVING VALUE: a harvest, a rate or a launch shifts with a factor one cannot fix.
branches.cn: 变动的值：收成、速率或发射，随一个无法固定的因素起落。

branches.en: THE TRUSTED PERSON: a handbook's sources and a volunteer at the door are relied on to hold.
branches.cn: 被信任的人：手册的来源与门口的志愿者，被指望守住。

branches.en: THE HELD HABIT: a pill that must be taken before sleep arrives.
branches.cn: 被抓住的习惯：不吃药就睡不着的夜晚。

intro.en: The family hangs from a Latin weighing verb; the prefix points downward, and the endings name the state, the person and the negation.
intro.cn: 这个词族挂在拉丁语「称重、悬挂」动词上；前缀指向下方，词尾命名状态、人与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere and dependere passed through French into English, which added its own endings and its own negative prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「悬挂」与「依附」动词经法语进入英语，英语加上自己的词尾与否定前缀。

items.example: It marks the weight as hanging down from a support.
items.exampleCN: 它标出重物从支撑处垂下。

items.example: The hanging verb at the base.
The direct source of the English verb.
The stem used in the modern phrase.
It forms the noun of reliance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「依赖」的名词。

items.example: It forms the adjective for one who relies.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「依赖者」的形容词。

items.example: It forms the adjective for what can be relied on.
It reverses the adjective into independence.

derivatives.zh: 由动词加状态名词尾构成，义为「依赖」
由动词加形容词尾构成，义为「依赖的」
由动词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可靠的」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「独立的」

definition_zh: 使疏远；使不友好；离间；（法律）转让（财产、权利）
definition_en: to make someone who was friendly or loyal become cold or hostile; in law, to transfer property or a right to another person
core_image: 把原本属于自己的人推到门外去
scene: 他一句玩笑得罪了半个团队，从此没人愿意跟他搭档。 His sarcasm began to alienate his closest colleagues.
sceneCN: 这里 alienate 是「使疏远」（第 1 个义项：让人从亲近转为冷淡或敌对）；句意为他的讥讽开始让最亲近的同事疏远他。核心画面是把原本属于自己的人推到门外去。

pos.zh: 使疏远；使不友好；离间；转让

derivatives.zh: 加 -ion 构成，义为「疏远；异化」
过去分词作形容词，义为「感到被疏远的」
同根形容词，义为「外国的；陌生的」

senses.title: To turn closeness into distance
senses.definition: to make someone who was friendly or loyal become cold, hostile or withdrawn, usually by your own behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 让原本友好或忠诚的人变得冷淡、敌对或退缩，通常由自己的行为造成
senses.example: The new rules alienated the very staff they were meant to help.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定反而让本该受照顾的员工疏远了。
senses.why: Alien means belonging to another, so alienate is to make someone into an outsider: you push a person who was yours across the boundary.
senses.whyCN: alien 意为「属于别人的」，所以 alienate 就是把某人变成外人：你把原本属于自己的人推过了界线。

senses.title: To transfer ownership away
senses.definition: in law, to transfer property or a right to another person, the older and technical sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 法律上把财产或权利转移给他人，是该词更古老、更专业的用法
senses.example: The trust forbids the heir to alienate the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 信托禁止继承人转让这份地产。
senses.why: This is the literal core: to make a thing alien, that is, the property of someone else, which is exactly what a legal transfer does.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：让某物变成 alien「别人的」，而法律上的转让做的正是这件事。

intro.en: Alienate comes straight from Latin alienus, belonging to another: to alienate is to make someone or something into the property of another, whether the loyalty of a friend or a piece of land.
intro.cn: alienate 直接来自拉丁语 alienus「属于别人的」：alienate 就是把某人或某物变成别人的，无论是朋友的忠诚还是一块土地。

items.en: Latin alius meant other or another, the root behind alias, alibi and alter.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alius 意为「其他、另一个」，是 alias、alibi 与 alter 背后的词根。

items.en: From alius came alienus, belonging to another person, hence foreign or strange.
items.cn: 由 alius 派生出 alienus「属于别人的」，因此引申为外国的、陌生的。

items.en: The verb alienare meant to transfer ownership, and also to estrange the affection of a person.
items.cn: 动词 alienare 意为转移所有权，也指使人的感情疏远。

items.en: Its past participle alienatus carried both senses, legal transfer and emotional estrangement.
items.cn: 其过去分词 alienatus 同时承载两义：法律转让与感情疏远。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the fourteenth century, first in law and soon after in descriptions of friendship.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入该词，先用于法律，随后用于描述友情。

items.en: Modern use favours the emotional sense, while the legal sense survives in deeds and in the noun alienation.
items.cn: 现代用法偏重感情义，法律义则保留在契据与名词 alienation 中。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ali- family of otherness; the near-meaning group lists other verbs for pushing people away.
note.cn: 形近组保留表示「他者」的 ali- 词族；近义组列出其他表示「把人推开」的动词。

entries.definition: Belonging to another place or person.
entries.definitionCN: 属于别处或别人的。

entries.definition: The state of being isolated or estranged.
entries.definitionCN: 被孤立或疏远的状态。

entries.definition: A false or alternative name.
entries.definitionCN: 假名或别名。

entries.definition: A claim of being elsewhere when a crime occurred.
entries.definitionCN: 声称案发时身在别处的说法。

entries.definition: To cause someone to become unfriendly.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人变得不友好。

entries.definition: To keep yourself apart from someone.
entries.definitionCN: 让自己与某人保持距离。

entries.definition: To leave someone alone and unsupported.
entries.definitionCN: 让某人孤立无援。

entries.definition: To make someone lose loyalty.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人失去忠诚。

normalIntro.en: Alienate is alien plus -ate: to make someone alien, an outsider, to you.
normalIntro.cn: alienate 就是 alien 加 -ate：把某人变成 alien，即变成你的外人。

normal.en: Alien means other, so alienate means to make other: the friend becomes a stranger.
normal.cn: alien 意为「他者」，所以 alienate 就是「使他者化」：朋友变成了陌生人。

normal.en: -ate turns the adjective into a verb, as in activate and isolate.
normal.cn: -ate 把形容词变成动词，如 activate、isolate。

normal.en: You alienate someone by your behaviour; you feel alienated by theirs.
normal.cn: 你的行为让别人疏远你；别人的行为让你感到被疏远。

normal.en: In law alienate simply means transfer, so alienate property is sell or give it away.
normal.cn: 法律上 alienate 就是转让，所以 alienate property 是卖掉或送出财产。

normal.en: The noun is alienation, not alienment: remember the -ation ending.
normal.cn: 名词是 alienation，不是 alienment：记住 -ation 这个词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a friend stepping across a line drawn on the floor and not coming back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个朋友跨过地上画的一条线，再也没有回来。

abstract.en: Imagine a door closing slowly between two people who used to share a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在两个曾同住一屋的人之间缓缓关上。

abstract.en: Think of a deed handing your land to the name of a stranger.
abstract.cn: 想象一纸契据把你的土地转到一个陌生人名下。

examples.en: Constant criticism will alienate even your supporters.
examples.cn: 不断的批评连你的支持者也会疏远。

examples.en: She felt alienated by the office gossip.
examples.cn: 办公室的闲言碎语让她感到被疏远。

examples.en: The clause prevents the owner from alienating the land.
examples.cn: 该条款阻止业主转让这块土地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诶里诶内特」——诶（a）里（li）诶（e）内特（nate）：把里面的人推到外面去，就是使疏远、离间。

root: 拉丁语 alius「其他」派生出 alienus「属于别人的」，加动词后缀构成 alienare「转让、使疏远」，其过去分词 alienatus 经中古英语 alienaten 进入现代英语成为 alienate，字面即「使成为他者」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses move something across a boundary: the emotional one pushes a person out of your circle, and the legal one pushes a property out of your name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是把某样东西推过界线：感情义把人推出你的圈子，法律义把财产推出你的名下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pushing what was yours across the boundary
core.cn: 核心意象：把原本属于你的推过界线

branches.en: A joke that costs you a friend.
branches.cn: 一个让你失去朋友的玩笑。

branches.en: Rules that push loyal staff away.
branches.cn: 把忠诚员工推开的规定。

branches.en: A deed that moves land to a new name.
branches.cn: 把土地转到新名下的契据。

branches.en: A right signed over to another party.
branches.cn: 签字让给另一方的权利。

branches.en: Both make what was yours into the property of another.
branches.cn: 两者都把原本属于你的变成别人的。

intro.en: Alienate keeps the ali- root of otherness and adds -ate to make a verb, with -ation available for the resulting state.
intro.cn: alienate 保留表示「他者」的 ali- 词根，加 -ate 构成动词，并可用 -ation 表示由此产生的状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin alius gave alienus, alienare and alienatus; English took the participle and kept both of its senses.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alius 派生出 alienus、alienare 与 alienatus；英语取用其分词，并保留了它的两个义项。

latinEntries.example: Alius is the root of the ali- family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: alius 是 ali- 词族的词根。
alienus 产生 alien 与 alienate。

latinEntries.example: Alienatus is the direct source of alienate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: alienatus 是 alienate 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 陶瓷的；陶瓷制品；陶瓷材料
definition_en: made of fired clay or of a similar inorganic material; a ceramic object or material
core_image: 一只上釉的白瓷碗放在灯下，釉面反出冷光，旁边是一片未上釉的灰坯
scene: 工程师把一小片烧成的材料放进高温炉，测试它能否承受骤冷。 The engineer placed a ceramic sample in the furnace to test how it survived sudden cooling.
sceneCN: 这里 ceramic 指「陶瓷材料」（第 3 个义项：经高温烧结的无机非金属材料）；句意为工程师把一片陶瓷样品放入炉中，测试它在骤冷后的状态。图中可辨识物件：高温炉、样品夹、温度表、冷却槽。

pos.zh: 陶瓷制品；陶瓷材料（常用复数指器物）

derivatives.zh: 陶瓷工艺；陶瓷学（加 -s 构成学科名）
以陶瓷方式；在陶瓷方面

senses.title: Made of fired clay
senses.definition: made of clay shaped and hardened by firing
senses.definitionCN: 由黏土塑形并经火烧硬制成的
senses.example: The floor was covered with ceramic tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 地面铺着瓷砖。
senses.why: ceramic is the adjective from the Greek word for potter's clay, so its first job is to describe clay ware.
senses.whyCN: ceramic 是来自希腊语「陶土」一词的形容词，因此首要用途是描述陶制器物。

senses.title: Relating to the ceramic arts
senses.definition: connected with the art and craft of making clay and porcelain objects
senses.definitionCN: 与制作陶器和瓷器的艺术手艺相关
senses.example: The gallery devotes one room to ceramic art.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊用一间展厅陈列陶瓷艺术。
senses.why: museums and studios use the adjective to mark the whole field rather than one object.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆与工作室用这个形容词标注整个领域，而不是单件器物。

senses.title: An engineered inorganic material
senses.definition: a hard, heat-resistant material made by firing inorganic powders, used in engineering
senses.definitionCN: 由无机粉末烧结而成、坚硬耐热的材料，用于工程
senses.example: A ceramic coating protects the turbine blade from heat.
senses.exampleCN: 一层陶瓷涂层保护涡轮叶片免受高温。
senses.why: materials science widened the word from pots to any fired inorganic solid with useful hardness.
senses.whyCN: 材料科学把这个词从陶罐扩展到任何烧成的、具备可用硬度的无机固体。

senses.title: A ceramic object, usually in the plural
senses.definition: an object made of fired clay or porcelain, often spoken of in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 用陶土或瓷土烧成的物件，常以复数形式出现
senses.example: Each ceramic is tested for porosity before packing.
senses.exampleCN: 每件陶瓷制品在包装前都要检测孔隙率。
senses.why: the countable noun turns the material name into one manufactured item.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词用法把材料名转化为一件制成品。

senses.title: Building ware such as tiles and sanitary fittings
senses.definition: fired clay products used in construction, such as tiles, sinks and toilets
senses.definitionCN: 用于建筑的烧制黏土产品，如瓷砖、水槽与便器
senses.example: The bathroom uses ceramic fittings throughout.
senses.exampleCN: 浴室全部使用陶瓷洁具。
senses.why: construction speaks of ceramic rather than pottery because the products are industrial, not artisanal.
senses.whyCN: 建筑行业说「陶瓷」而不说「陶器」，因为这些产品是工业品，不是手工艺品。

senses.title: Material used in dentistry and medicine
senses.definition: a fired inorganic material used for crowns, implants and medical devices
senses.definitionCN: 用于牙冠、植入体与医疗器械的烧制无机材料
senses.example: The crown is made of a translucent ceramic that matches the tooth.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗牙冠用一种与牙齿颜色相近的半透明陶瓷制成。
senses.why: dentistry needed materials that are hard, inert and tooth-coloured, and ceramic supplied all three.
senses.whyCN: 牙科需要坚硬、惰性且颜色接近牙齿的材料，陶瓷正好三者兼具。

senses.title: The glazed surface of such ware
senses.definition: the glassy fired coating on clay ware, considered as a finish
senses.definitionCN: 陶器表面烧成的玻璃质涂层，作为一种饰面
senses.example: A blue ceramic glaze ran down the side of the bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 一层蓝色釉顺着碗壁流下。
senses.why: the adjective came to describe the glaze itself, since the finish is what the eye actually sees.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也用来描述釉本身，因为肉眼真正看到的就是这层饰面。

senses.title: Hard plates used in armour
senses.definition: a hard ceramic plate used in protective armour to stop projectiles
senses.definitionCN: 用于防护装甲、阻挡弹丸的硬质陶瓷板
senses.example: The vest carries a ceramic plate over the chest.
senses.exampleCN: 这件防弹背心在胸前装有一块陶瓷板。
senses.why: the engineering sense narrowed again in armour design, where extreme hardness matters more than heat resistance.
senses.whyCN: 工程义在装甲设计中再次收窄，那里极致的硬度比耐热更重要。

intro.en: Ceramic comes from Greek keramikos 'of pottery', from keramos 'potter's clay, pottery', and entered English through learned Latin and French forms in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ceramic 来自希腊 keramikos「陶器的」，源于 keramos「陶土、陶器」，十九世纪经学术拉丁语与法语形式进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Keramos named potter's clay and pottery. Its earlier origin is not established; a link to kerannynai 'to mix' is a hypothesis, and a pre-Greek source is also proposed.
items.cn: keramos 指陶土与陶器。其更早来源没有定论；把它联系到 kerannynai「混合」只是假说，也有人提出源自前希腊语。

items.en: Keramikos meant 'of pottery' and was used of the potters' quarter and of clay ware generally.
items.cn: keramikos 意为「陶器的」，用于指陶工区，也泛指陶制器物。

items.en: Learned Latin took the Greek adjective as ceramicus and the noun as ceramica, keeping the Greek root intact.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语把这个希腊形容词写作 ceramicus，名词写作 ceramica，希腊词根原样保留。

items.en: English adopted ceramic in the nineteenth century as the scientific and artistic term for fired clay ware.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪采用 ceramic，作为烧制陶器的科学与艺术术语。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was extended to engineering ceramics, dental ceramics and armour plates.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词扩展到工程陶瓷、牙科陶瓷与装甲板。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of keramos is unsettled, so any older form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：keramos 的前希腊语历史没有定论，为它提出的更早形态均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes with different roots or endings; group two holds the ware names that are often used as if they were synonyms of ceramic.
note.cn: 第一组是词根或词尾不同却形近的词；第二组是常被当作 ceramic 同义词使用的器物名。

entries.definition: The plural noun for the art and science of ceramic ware, or for the objects themselves; it is not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指陶瓷艺术与科学的复数名词，也指器物本身；它不是形容词。

entries.definition: A maker or student of ceramics; the ending marks a person, not a material.
entries.definitionCN: 陶瓷艺人或研究者；词尾标出的是人，不是材料。

entries.definition: The protein of hair, horn and nails, from Greek keras 'horn'; it looks close but has no connection with clay.
entries.definitionCN: 毛发、角与指甲中的蛋白质，来自希腊 keras「角」；形近，但与黏土毫无关系。

entries.definition: A second spelling of the person noun, built with -icist rather than -ist; both are current.
entries.definitionCN: 指人名词的另一种拼法，用 -icist 而非 -ist；两种写法都在使用。

entries.definition: The everyday mass noun for fired clay ware and the craft that makes it; ceramic is its technical and industrial counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指烧制陶器及其手艺的日常名词；ceramic 是它的技术与工业对应词。

entries.definition: Porous clay ware fired at a lower temperature, usually glazed to hold water.
entries.definitionCN: 较低温度烧成的多孔陶器，通常上釉以防渗水。

entries.definition: Dense, non-porous clay ware fired high enough to be waterproof without glaze.
entries.definitionCN: 烧成温度较高、致密不渗水的陶器，无须上釉即可防水。

entries.definition: The finest ceramic ware, white and translucent, fired at very high temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 最精细的陶瓷，白色半透明，烧成温度极高。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes, real industrial phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语构词成分、真实工业短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek keramos 'potter's clay' plus -ic 'relating to': relating to clay ware.
normal.cn: 希腊 keramos「陶土」加 -ic「与……相关」：与陶制器物相关。

normal.en: The family runs ceramic, ceramics, ceramist, ceramicist, ceramically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ceramic、ceramics、ceramist、ceramicist、ceramically。

normal.en: Industry phrases mark the technical sense: advanced ceramic, ceramic coating, ceramic matrix.
normal.cn: 工业短语标出技术义：先进陶瓷、陶瓷涂层、陶瓷基体。

normal.en: Building suppliers speak of ceramic tiles and ceramic fittings, never of pottery tiles.
normal.cn: 建材商说瓷砖与陶瓷洁具，从不说「陶器砖」。

normal.en: Dentistry pairs the word with crown and implant: ceramic crown, ceramic implant.
normal.cn: 牙科把这个词与牙冠、植入体搭配：陶瓷冠、陶瓷植入体。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl so hard that it rings like a bell but shatters like glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗硬得敲起来像钟，却又能像玻璃一样碎裂。

abstract.en: Picture a heat shield that began as a lump of grey powder.
abstract.cn: 想象一块隔热罩，最初只是一团灰色粉末。

abstract.en: Picture a tooth rebuilt from the same stuff as a teacup.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗牙齿用与茶杯相同的材料重建。

examples.en: The façade is clad in ceramic panels that resist graffiti.
examples.cn: 外立面覆以抗涂鸦的陶瓷板。

examples.en: Ceramic bearings run smoothly without oil.
examples.cn: 陶瓷轴承无需润滑油即可平稳运转。

examples.en: The museum bought a set of ceramic vessels from the site.
examples.cn: 博物馆从该遗址购得一套陶瓷器皿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cera（蜡似的光）+ mic」——釉面像蜡一样发亮的东西 → 陶瓷

root: 希腊 keramos「陶土、陶器」→ keramikos「陶器的」→ 学术拉丁 ceramicus → 英语 ceramic。keramos 的更早来源不确定，与前希腊语或 kerannynai「混合」的联系均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from the potter's clay outward: the clay ware itself, the art, the engineered material, one object, building fittings, dental work, the glaze, and finally armour.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从陶土向外扩散：陶制器物本身、陶瓷艺术、工程材料、单件制品、建筑洁具、牙科修复、釉面，最后是装甲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft clay passing through fire and coming out hard, glossy and useful.
core.cn: 核心意象：柔软的黏土穿过火焰，出来时坚硬、光亮而有用。

branches.en: WARE: the adjective describes fired clay objects, and the countable noun names one of them.
branches.cn: 器物：形容词描述烧制的陶制品，可数名词则指其中一件。

branches.en: SURFACE AND ART: what the eye meets is the glaze, and the craft that produces it is ceramic art.
branches.cn: 表面与艺术：眼睛看到的是釉，制作釉面的手艺就是陶瓷艺术。

branches.en: ENGINEERING HARDNESS: the same material serves turbine blades and armour plates where hardness is the point.
branches.cn: 工程硬度：同一种材料用于涡轮叶片与装甲板，那里关键就是硬度。

branches.en: BUILDING: tiles and sanitary fittings carry the word into construction as an industrial category.
branches.cn: 建筑：瓷砖与洁具把这个词作为工业类别带入建筑业。

branches.en: BODY: dentistry borrows the material because it is hard, inert and close in colour to enamel.
branches.cn: 身体：牙科借用这种材料，因为它坚硬、惰性且颜色接近牙釉质。

intro.en: Ceramic is a Greek root with a Greek adjective ending, routed through learned Latin and then into English.
intro.cn: ceramic 是希腊词根加希腊形容词词尾，经学术拉丁语转入英语。

latinIntro.en: Learned Latin kept the Greek forms as ceramicus and ceramica; English drew ceramic from them and later added -s to make the field name.
latinIntro.cn: 学术拉丁语保留希腊形式写作 ceramicus 与 ceramica；英语由此取得 ceramic，后来又加 -s 构成学科名。

items.example: The root names the material before the object.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根先命名材料，再命名器物。

items.example: The suffix turns the material into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把材料变成形容词。

items.meaning: relating to fired clay; made of it
items.example: A ceramic liner protects the pipe.

items.meaning: the field, or a set of objects
items.example: The ending makes ceramics a subject name.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使 ceramics 成为学科名。

items.meaning: the art and science of ceramic ware
items.example: Ceramics is taught in the engineering faculty.

items.meaning: a maker or student of ceramics
items.example: The ceramist tested three new glazes.
items.exampleCN: 这位陶艺家试了三种新釉。

items.example: The ceramicist works mainly in porcelain.
items.exampleCN: 这位陶艺家主要用瓷土创作。

items.meaning: a glassy fired coating on clay ware
items.example: A ceramic glaze sealed the porous body.
items.exampleCN: 一层陶瓷釉封住了多孔的坯体。

latinEntries.structure: ceramica, ceramicae (f., first declension, Latinized Greek)

definition_zh: 地质学；地质构造；地质条件
definition_en: the science that studies the earth's rocks, layers and history, or the actual rock structure of a particular region
core_image: 一本摊开的图册，左页画着地层剖面，右页写着年代
scene: 这里指「地质学」。 The geology of the basin is dominated by thick sandstone laid down in a shallow sea.
sceneCN: 这里 geology 是「地质构造」（第 2 个义项：某地区的岩层组成与层序）；句意：这个盆地的地质以浅海中沉积的厚层砂岩为主。图中可辨识物件：盆地剖面、砂岩层、化石、年代柱、野外记录本。

pos.zh: 地质学；地质构造；地质条件（作学科名时不可数，指某地构造时可加不定冠词）

forms.label: 复数（指多地区的地质构造）

senses.title: The science of the solid earth
senses.titleCN: 地质学：研究固体地球的学科
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies rocks, minerals, strata and the history of the earth
senses.definitionCN: 研究岩石、矿物、地层与地球历史的科学分支
senses.example: Geology explains both the mountain and the sea floor beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学既能解释这座山，也能解释它旁边的海底。
senses.why: geology joins Greek gē 'earth' with -logia 'account, study', so the word's first sense is simply 'the account of the earth'.
senses.whyCN: geology 由希腊 gē“大地”与 -logia“论述、研究”构成，因此其第一义项就是“关于大地的论述”。

senses.title: A region's rock structure
senses.titleCN: 某地区的地质构造：那里的岩层组成
senses.definition: the actual arrangement of rocks and strata in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 某地岩石与地层的实际排列方式
senses.example: The geology here is simple: flat limestone over granite.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的地质很简单：平坦的石灰岩覆盖在花岗岩上。
senses.why: The same noun shifts from the subject to its object, as 'biology' can mean the living world of a region; here it names what the ground is made of.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从学科转向其对象，正如 biology 也可指某地的生物界；这里它指地下由什么构成。

senses.title: Ground conditions for building
senses.titleCN: 地质条件：工程眼中的地下状况
senses.definition: the underground conditions that affect construction, drilling or tunnelling
senses.definitionCN: 影响施工、钻探或掘进的地下条件
senses.example: The engineers ordered a report on the site's geology before bidding.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在投标前要求提交该场地的地质条件报告。
senses.why: Practical builders need to know what will resist or collapse; the abstract science becomes a site-specific condition.
senses.whyCN: 实际施工者需要知道什么会承重、什么会坍塌；抽象学问于是变成具体场地的条件。

senses.title: The subject as taught
senses.titleCN: 作为课程的地质学：大学里的一门学科
senses.definition: the school or university subject and its departments and degrees
senses.definitionCN: 中小学或大学里的课程，及其院系与学位
senses.example: She took geology as her major and never left the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她主修地质学，此后从未离开这个领域。
senses.why: Any science also exists as a curriculum; the noun covers lecture halls and degrees, not only research.
senses.whyCN: 任何科学也以课程形式存在；这个名词覆盖讲堂与学位，而不只是研究。

senses.title: Geology of other worlds
senses.titleCN: 行星地质：别的天体的岩层研究
senses.definition: the study of the solid surface and interior of moons, planets and asteroids
senses.definitionCN: 对卫星、行星与小行星固体表面与内部的研究
senses.example: Planetary geology compares Martian dunes with desert sand on earth.
senses.exampleCN: 行星地质学把火星沙丘与地球沙漠的沙作比较。
senses.why: Rock physics is not earth-bound, so the discipline's name travels to any solid body with a surface to read.
senses.whyCN: 岩石物理并不限于地球，因此这门学科的名字可以迁移到任何有表面可读的固体天体。

senses.title: Economic geology
senses.titleCN: 经济地质：矿产与能源的成因研究
senses.definition: the branch concerned with the origin and location of ore, oil, gas and coal
senses.definitionCN: 研究矿石、石油、天然气与煤的成因与分布的分支
senses.example: Economic geology pointed the company to a copper belt nobody had mapped.
senses.exampleCN: 经济地质把这家公司引向一条此前无人测绘的铜矿带。
senses.why: If rocks concentrate metals and fuels, then understanding rock history is directly profitable, and the branch is named for that use.
senses.whyCN: 既然岩石会富集金属与燃料，理解岩石历史便直接有利可图，这一分支正因这种用途而得名。

senses.title: Environmental and water geology
senses.titleCN: 环境与水文地质：地下水与污染的研究
senses.definition: the branch dealing with groundwater, soil contamination and land stability
senses.definitionCN: 研究地下水、土壤污染与土地稳定性的分支
senses.example: Environmental geology traced the solvent plume to a leaking tank.
senses.exampleCN: 环境地质把这片溶剂羽流追溯到一只渗漏的储罐。
senses.why: Once pollution travels through pores and fractures, rock structure decides where it goes, so geology becomes an environmental tool.
senses.whyCN: 一旦污染物沿孔隙与裂隙运移，岩石结构就决定它的去向，地质学于是成为环境工具。

senses.title: The knowledge of a planet's structure
senses.titleCN: 地质知识体系：关于某天体构造的总认识
senses.definition: the accumulated body of knowledge about how a planet or moon is built
senses.definitionCN: 关于某行星或卫星如何构成的知识总汇
senses.example: What we call the geology of Mars rests on a few landers and many orbits.
senses.exampleCN: 我们所说的火星地质，只建立在少数着陆器与大量轨道观测之上。
senses.why: Beyond any single region or course, the noun can name everything known about one body's solid structure.
senses.whyCN: 超出单一地区或课程之外，这个名词还可指关于某一固体天体构造的全部已知。

intro.en: Geology is Greek in its parts (gē 'earth', -logia 'account') and modern in its meaning. Its Latinized form geologia appears in the 17th century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: geology 的构件属希腊语（gē“大地”、-logia“论述”），词义则是近代形成的。其拉丁化形式 geologia 于 17 世纪出现。年代为约数。

items.en: gē 'earth' plus logos 'word, account, reason' gives the combining form -logia, 'a speaking or writing about'. The classical compound geologia is rarely attested.
items.cn: gē“大地”加 logos“言词、记述、道理”构成组合成分 -logia，意为“关于……的言说或书写”。古典时期 geologia 这一复合词极少见。

items.en: geologia is used in 17th-century Latin for descriptions of the earth's materials, often in contrast with theology. Several writers used it separately.
items.cn: 17 世纪拉丁语用 geologia 指对地球物质的描述，常与神学相对。多位作者各自使用过该词。

items.en: In the late 18th century the word settled on strata and earth history, as field mapping and fossil correlation became standard methods.
items.cn: 18 世纪后期，随着野外填图与化石对比成为标准方法，该词固定为研究地层与地球历史的含义。

items.en: The 19th century multiplied its branches: stratigraphy, palaeontology, mineralogy and later geophysics, each keeping geology as the umbrella name.
items.cn: 19 世纪其分支大量增生：地层学、古生物学、矿物学，以及后来的地球物理学，都以 geology 作为统称。

items.en: Plate tectonics unified the science in the 1960s, and planetary geology extended the name to other bodies after the first lunar samples.
items.cn: 板块构造学说在 20 世纪 60 年代统一了这门科学；首批月球样品之后，行星地质又把这一名称扩展到其他天体。

items.en: The first appearance of geologia and the exact moment when it lost its broader 'natural philosophy of the earth' sense are both uncertain.
items.cn: geologia 的首见时间，以及它何时失去更宽泛的“地球自然哲学”含义，都存疑。

note.en: The first group holds forms and neighbours from the same stems; the second holds other earth-science disciplines that are often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干的形式与邻词；第二组是常与之混淆的其他地球科学学科。

entries.definition: The specialist who practises geology. Use the -ist form for people and the bare noun for the field.
entries.definitionCN: 从事地质学的专家；指人用 -ist 形式，指学科用本词。

entries.definition: Relating to geology, as in geological time or geological survey. It modifies nouns rather than naming the field.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，如地质年代、地质调查；它修饰名词，而非命名学科。

entries.definition: The study of places, climate and distribution, built on -graphy 'write'; geology reads what lies under the surface, geography describes what lies on it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地点、气候与分布，词基为 -graphy“书写”；地质学读地下，地理学描述地上。

entries.definition: The branch of geology and geography that studies landform origin; it is one subfield, not the whole science.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地貌成因的分支，横跨地质学与地理学；它只是一个子领域，而非整门科学。

entries.definition: The whole group of sciences about the planet, including atmosphere and oceans; geology is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 关于本行星的全部科学，包括大气与海洋；地质学是其中一员。

entries.definition: The study of strata and their correlation; a core method within geology rather than a synonym for it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地层及其对比；是地质学的核心方法，而非其同义词。

entries.definition: The measurement and modelling of the earth's fields and interior using physical methods; it overlaps geology but asks physical questions.
entries.definitionCN: 用物理方法测量并建模地球的场与内部；与地质学重叠，但提出的是物理问题。

entries.definition: The study of mineral composition and crystal structure; narrower than geology, which also covers strata and history.
entries.definitionCN: 研究矿物成分与晶体结构；比地质学窄，后者还覆盖地层与历史。

entries.definition: The study of climate, rivers and landforms at the surface; it meets geology but keeps its focus above ground.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地表的气候、河流与地貌；与地质学相接，但焦点保持在地上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: geo- 'earth' + -logy 'study': the study of the earth.
normal.cn: geo-“大地”+ -logy“研究”：研究大地的学问。

normal.en: Petroleum geology, engineering geology and glacial geology are the standard branch names.
normal.cn: 石油地质学、工程地质学、冰川地质学是标准的分支名称。

normal.en: The noun pattern is geology, geologist, geological; only the first names the field.
normal.cn: 名词序列是 geology、geologist、geological；只有第一个指学科。

normal.en: The phrase the geology of an area covers sense 2 and is the most common non-academic use.
normal.cn: the geology of an area 这一说法对应第 2 个义项，是最常见的非学术用法。

normal.en: geology studies stone; geography describes places; geometry measures shapes. Same prefix, three stems.
normal.cn: geology 研究石头，geography 描述地点，geometry 测量形状；同一前缀，三个不同词干。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every shelf is a rock layer and every book a fossil.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每一层书架都是一层岩石，每本书都是一块化石。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose second hand takes a million years to move once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟，秒针走一格要一百万年。

abstract.en: Picture a building site where the blueprints include what lies fifty metres down.
abstract.cn: 想象一处工地，图纸上连地下五十米的东西也要画出来。

examples.en: He studied geology because he wanted to know why the Alps are still rising.
examples.cn: 他学地质学，是因为想知道阿尔卑斯山为什么还在升高。

examples.en: The geology of the delta consists of river sand over marine clay.
examples.cn: 这个三角洲的地质由河流砂层覆盖海相黏土构成。

examples.en: Economic geology identified a gold-bearing quartz vein under the old mine.
examples.cn: 经济地质在旧矿下方识别出一条含金石英脉。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地（geo）层讲逻辑（logy）”——一层压一层自有道理 → geology 地质学、地质构造

root: 希腊 gē“大地”+ logos“言说、道理”（组合形式 -logia）→ 拉丁化 geologia；现代义为研究地层与地球历史。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one object: the layered ground. The name covers the science, the ground itself, the site report, the course, other worlds and its profitable branches.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一个对象展开：层状的地下。这个名称覆盖学科、地下本身、场地报告、课程、别的天体，以及它有利可图的分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cross-section of ground in which each band is a period of time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅地下剖面，每一条带都是一段时间。

branches.en: SCIENCE AND OBJECT: the discipline and a region's actual layers are the two faces of one noun.
branches.cn: 学科与对象：这门学问与某地实际的岩层，是同一个名词的两面。

branches.en: SITE REPORT: what the science knows becomes a practical condition at a building site.
branches.cn: 场地报告：这门学问所知转化成工地上的实际条件。

branches.en: CURRICULUM: the field also exists as lectures, departments and degrees.
branches.cn: 课程：这一领域也以讲座、院系与学位的形式存在。

branches.en: OTHER BODIES: the name travels to any solid world, and also names the total knowledge of one such world.
branches.cn: 别的天体：这个名称可迁移到任何固体世界，也可指关于某一世界的全部认识。

branches.en: USEFUL BRANCHES: rocks hold fuel and ore, and also carry water and pollution.
branches.cn: 有用的分支：岩石既藏燃料与矿石，也输送地下水与污染。

intro.en: Geology is a two-part Greek compound, geo- 'earth' plus -logy 'study or account'. Both parts remain productive in modern technical English.
intro.cn: geology 是两段式希腊复合词：geo-“大地”加 -logy“研究或论述”。两部分在现代技术英语中仍能产。

latinIntro.en: The -logy family reached English chiefly through Latin and French: biology, ecology, theology, psychology and technology all follow the same model.
latinIntro.cn: -logy 词族主要经拉丁语与法语进入英语：biology、ecology、theology、psychology、technology 都遵循同一模式。

items.meaning: the science of the earth's solid matter
items.meaningCN: 研究地球固体物质的科学
items.example: Geology is the backbone of the mining programme.
items.exampleCN: 地质学是该采矿计划的主干。

items.example: Two geologists checked the outcrop before the blast.
items.exampleCN: 爆破前两名地质学家检查了露头。

items.example: The geological map covers the whole catchment.
items.exampleCN: 这幅地质图覆盖整个流域。

items.example: Geologically, the island is a young volcano.
items.exampleCN: 从地质上看，这座岛是一座年轻的火山。

items.example: Geophysics mapped the water table by sound waves.
items.exampleCN: 地球物理学用声波测绘了地下水位。

items.example: Geochemistry dates the granite by its isotopes.
items.exampleCN: 地球化学用同位素测定花岗岩年龄。

items.meaning: the description and ordering of strata
items.meaningCN: 对地层的描述与层序研究
items.example: Stratigraphy places the ash layer between two lavas.
items.exampleCN: 地层学把火山灰层置于两层熔岩之间。

items.example: Mineralogy identified the green crystal as olivine.
items.exampleCN: 矿物学把那颗绿色晶体鉴定为橄榄石。

latinEntries.meaning: an account of the earth (17th-century Latin)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 关于大地的论述（17 世纪拉丁语）

definition_zh: adj. 平常的 n. 老生常谈；平常事
definition_en: ordinary and not interesting; also an everyday remark
core_image: 街头人人都在扫码付款，没人再抬头看
scene: 手机支付如今已很平常，不再让人惊讶。 Paying by phone is now commonplace and surprises no one.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：commonplace 指平常的；句意是手机支付如今已很平常，不再让人惊讶。

senses.title: Ordinary and unremarkable
senses.definition: so usual that it no longer attracts attention
senses.definitionCN: 平常到不再引人注意
senses.example: Electric cars are becoming commonplace.
senses.exampleCN: 电动车正变得司空见惯。
senses.why: English calqued Latin locus communis, a common place.
senses.whyCN: 英语仿译拉丁语 locus communis（共同之处）。

senses.title: A trite remark
senses.definition: a remark that is true but dull because it is repeated
senses.definitionCN: 因反复而显得乏味的正确说法
senses.example: His speech was full of commonplaces.
senses.exampleCN: 他的演讲满是老生常谈。
senses.why: The noun sense came from rhetorical handbooks.
senses.whyCN: 名词义来自修辞手册。

intro.en: Commonplace translates a Latin phrase meaning a shared place.
intro.cn: commonplace 直译拉丁语中「共同的处所」这一短语。

items.en: Locus means a place.
items.cn: locus 意为地方。

items.en: Communis means shared.
items.cn: communis 意为共同的。

items.en: The phrase names a general topic.
items.cn: 这一短语指一般性话题。

items.en: English coined commonplace from the phrase.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语由该短语造出 commonplace。

items.en: It came to mean dull and trite.
items.cn: 十九世纪它获得「平庸陈腐」义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the common- opening; the near-meaning group names the ordinary.
note.cn: 形近组共享 common- 开头；近义组列出普通之物。

entries.definition: A person without a title.
entries.definitionCN: 平民。

entries.definition: A political community.
entries.definitionCN: 联邦。

entries.definition: Shared or usual.
entries.definitionCN: 常见的。

entries.definition: Not special.
entries.definitionCN: 普通的。

entries.definition: Happening each day.
entries.definitionCN: 日常的。

entries.definition: Done as a habit.
entries.definitionCN: 例行的。

normalIntro.en: A commonplace is literally a common place, so common it is dull.
normalIntro.cn: commonplace 字面就是「共同之处」，共同到显得乏味。

normal.en: Locus means place.
normal.cn: locus 意为地方。

normal.en: Communis means shared.
normal.cn: communis 意为共同的。

normal.en: A common place is a shared topic.
normal.cn: common place 是共同话题。

normal.en: So commonplace means ordinary.
normal.cn: 因此 commonplace 意为平常。

normal.en: A dull saying is a commonplace.
normal.cn: 乏味的说法就是老生常谈。

abstract.en: A street everyone walks past.
abstract.cn: 人人走过却不看的街。

abstract.en: A phrase worn smooth.
abstract.cn: 被磨得光滑的一句话。

abstract.en: Rain on a Tuesday.
abstract.cn: 周二的雨。

examples.en: Smartphones are now commonplace in schools.
examples.cn: 智能手机在学校已很常见。

examples.en: The essay repeats one commonplace after another.
examples.cn: 这篇文章堆满老生常谈。

examples.en: Such accidents are sadly commonplace.
examples.cn: 这类事故不幸地很常见。

dict_mnemonic.text: common（共同）+ place（地方）→ 人人共有的地方，即平常事、老生常谈。

root: 拉丁 locus communis（共同之处）→ 英语 common + place → commonplace

sensesIntro.en: Common enough to be dull, whether an event or a phrase.
sensesIntro.cn: 平常到乏味，不论是事件还是说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street scene no one bothers to look at
core.cn: 核心意象：没人愿意多看一眼的街景

branches.en: A phone paying for coffee.
branches.cn: 用手机买咖啡。

branches.en: An event nobody reports.
branches.cn: 无人报道的事件。

branches.en: A speech of worn phrases.
branches.cn: 满是旧话的演讲。

branches.en: A saying everyone knows.
branches.cn: 人人都知道的说法。

branches.en: The usual, as event or as remark.
branches.cn: 平常之物，无论事件或说法。

intro.en: Commonplace joins two plain English words; the list adds everyday pieces.
intro.cn: commonplace 由两个普通英语词合成；下面列出日常词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin communis is shared, locus is a place, and ordo is order.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 communis 意为共同的，locus 意为地方，ordo 意为次序。

latinEntries.exampleCN: locus communis 变成英语 commonplace。
communis 产生 common 与 community。
ordo 产生 order 与 ordinary。

definition_zh: 手风琴；可折叠的
definition_en: a musical instrument with a folding bellows and keyboard, or a pleated folding style
core_image: 一叠风箱被拉开又合上，挤出一个个音
scene: 街角艺人把琴抱在胸前，一拉一合，风箱像手风琴一样伸展。 He played an accordion on the corner every evening.
sceneCN: 这里 accordion 是「手风琴」（第 1 个义项：带折叠风箱的键盘乐器）；句意为他每天傍晚在街角拉手风琴。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「手风琴演奏者」

senses.title: A folding musical instrument
senses.definition: a portable instrument with a bellows and keys that produces sound when squeezed
senses.definitionCN: 带风箱与键、挤压发声的便携乐器
senses.example: She learned the accordion from her grandfather.
senses.exampleCN: 她跟祖父学拉手风琴。
senses.why: The name came from German Akkordion, a coined word for an instrument whose parts are in accord, or harmony.
senses.whyCN: 这一名称来自德语 Akkordion，是为这种「各部件相和」的乐器造的词。

senses.title: A pleated or folding form
senses.definition: of a file, door, or sheet, folding in and out like a bellows
senses.definitionCN: 指文件夹、门或纸张像风箱一样来回折叠
senses.example: She keeps receipts in an accordion folder by month.
senses.exampleCN: 她按月把收据放在风琴式文件夹里。
senses.why: Because the bellows folds in deep pleats, everyday objects that fold the same way borrow the instrument's name.
senses.whyCN: 由于风箱折成深褶，以同样方式折叠的日常物件便借用了这件乐器的名字。

intro.en: Accordion is a nineteenth-century coinage from German Akkordion, built on Accord, 'harmony'.
intro.cn: accordion 是十九世纪由德语 Akkordion 造出的词，建立在 Accord（和谐）之上。

items.en: cor meant 'heart', the root behind accord.
items.cn: cor 意为「心」，是 accord 背后的词根。

items.en: accordare meant 'to bring into harmony'.
items.cn: accordare 意为「使和谐」。

items.en: Akkord meant a chord or a harmonious combination of notes.
items.cn: Akkord 意为和弦或和谐的音组合。

items.en: The name was coined for an instrument combining reed pipes and bellows.
items.cn: 这一名称是为结合簧管与风箱的乐器而造。

items.en: English borrowed accordion as the instrument spread across Europe.
items.cn: 随着乐器传遍欧洲，英语借入 accordion。

items.en: Modern usage adds the pleated-file and folding-door senses.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了风琴式文件夹与折叠门义。

note.en: The first group gathers the player word, the root noun, and the look-alike; the second gathers words for the instrument and for folding.
note.cn: 第一组收演奏者、同源名词与形近词；第二组收表示乐器与折叠的词。

entries.definition: A person who plays the accordion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手风琴演奏者」。

entries.definition: An agreement or harmony, the word behind the name.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「协议、和谐」，名称所本之词。

entries.definition: A folder with pleated pockets.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「风琴式文件夹」。

entries.definition: A similar squeezebox instrument with a different mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「六角手风琴」，机理不同的同类乐器。

entries.definition: A small mouth organ, also built on a harmony word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「口琴」，名称同样出自「和谐」。

entries.definition: An adjective for fabric folded into regular ridges.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有褶的」。

entries.definition: An adjective for something made to fold up.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可折叠的」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the harmony name and the street-musician scene; the abstract hooks picture a bellows opening and closing in pleats.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「和谐」名称与街头艺人场景；抽象记忆点想象风箱一开一合的褶皱。

normal.en: Accordion is built on accord, 'harmony': notes and parts that agree.
normal.cn: accordion 建立在 accord（和谐）之上：相互协调的音与部件。

normal.en: Play the accordion uses the definite article in English.
normal.cn: play the accordion 在英语中要加定冠词。

normal.en: An accordion file folds in and out like bellows.
normal.cn: an accordion file 像风箱一样折叠。

normal.en: The player is an accordionist.
normal.cn: 演奏者是 accordionist。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with accord, the agreement word.
normal.cn: 不要与表示协议的 accord 混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a street musician squeezing a bellows against his chest.
abstract.cn: 想象街头艺人把风箱抱在胸前挤压。

abstract.en: Picture a file with pockets that spread open like stairs.
abstract.cn: 想象文件夹的袋口像台阶一样张开。

abstract.en: Picture a folding door narrowing the room in pleats.
abstract.cn: 想象折叠门以褶皱把房间收窄。

examples.en: The band includes a fiddler and an accordion player.
examples.cn: 乐队里有一位小提琴手和一位手风琴手。

examples.en: He filed the invoices in an accordion folder.
examples.cn: 他把发票放进风琴式文件夹。

examples.en: The accordion door saves space in the narrow hall.
examples.cn: 折叠门为狭窄走廊节省空间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿科迪昂」——一叠风箱拉开来全是褶，合起来就成调。

root: 德语 Akkordion，源自 Accord（和谐）；核心义是「以折叠风箱挤出和谐音的乐器」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the instrument itself, to anything folded in the same pleated way.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从乐器本身，走到任何以同样褶皱方式折叠的物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bellows opening into pleats and closing into a note
core.cn: 核心意象：风箱张开成褶、合拢成音

branches.en: The squeezebox instrument with keys and bellows.
branches.cn: 带键与风箱的便携乐器。

branches.en: A file or door that folds like a bellows.
branches.cn: 像风箱一样折叠的文件夹或门。

branches.en: The instrument's shape gives the folding objects their name.
branches.cn: 乐器的形状给了折叠物件名称。

branches.en: The deep pleats are the shared picture.
branches.cn: 深褶皱是共享的图景。

branches.en: One word covers a sound and a silhouette.
branches.cn: 同一个词覆盖一种声音与一种轮廓。

intro.en: The word joins the harmony noun with a Greek-style ending, and its family adds the player suffix and the related accord words.
intro.cn: 这个词把「和谐」名词与希腊式词尾结合，词族另加演奏者后缀与相关 accord 词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin heart noun cor stands behind accord and thus behind accordion, so those entries are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「心」名词 cor 在 accord 之后，也就在 accordion 之后，因此收录这些条目。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「手风琴演奏者」

definition_zh: 传记；传记文学；生平记述
definition_en: an account of a person's life written by someone else
core_image: 一个人的一生被装订成厚厚一册，由他人执笔
scene: 博物馆纪念展旁边开了一家小书店。 She spent five years writing the biography of the poet.
sceneCN: 这里 biography 是「传记」（第 1 个义项：他人所写的生平记述）；句意是她花五年为诗人立传。

derivatives.zh: biography 的形容词，义为「传记的；关于生平的」
biography 的缩略，义为「小传；简介」

senses.title: A written life of a person
senses.definition: a book or article telling the story of someone's life, written by another
senses.definitionCN: 由他人执笔、讲述某人生平的书籍或文章
senses.example: She spent five years writing the biography of the poet.
senses.exampleCN: 她花五年为诗人立传。
senses.why: Greek bios means life and graphein means to write: the writing of a life.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 bios 意为「生命」，graphein 意为「书写」，合即「书写一生」。

senses.title: Lives as a literary genre
senses.definition: the literary genre of life-writing as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 作为文体的传记写作整体
senses.example: Biography blends history with storytelling.
senses.exampleCN: 传记文学融历史与叙事于一体。
senses.why: One written life stands for all life-writing.
senses.whyCN: 一部传记可代指整个传记文体。

senses.title: The events of a life
senses.definition: the course of a person's life as a set of facts
senses.definitionCN: 作为事实总和的某人一生经历
senses.example: The film sticks closely to the scientist's biography.
senses.exampleCN: 影片紧贴这位科学家的真实生平。
senses.why: The life itself can be called by the word for its record.
senses.whyCN: 一生本身可借其记录之名来称呼。

senses.title: A short life-sketch
senses.definition: a brief account of a life, as in a program or application
senses.definitionCN: 简短生平介绍，如节目册或申请材料中的
senses.example: Each speaker's biography appeared in the program.
senses.exampleCN: 每位讲者的小传都印在手册里。
senses.why: The full book shrinks to a paragraph.
senses.whyCN: 整部书缩为一段文字。

senses.title: Ancient lives tradition
senses.definition: the classical tradition of lives, from Plutarch onward
senses.definitionCN: 自普鲁塔克以降的古典传记传统
senses.example: His essay compares ancient biography with modern.
senses.exampleCN: 他的文章比较古今传记传统。
senses.why: The genre names its own history.
senses.whyCN: 文体之名亦涵盖其自身的历史。

senses.title: A life used for interpretation
senses.definition: a person's life used to explain their work or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 以作者生平解读其作品或思想
senses.example: The critic rejected purely biographical reading.
senses.exampleCN: 这位批评家拒绝纯传记式解读。
senses.why: The life story becomes a critical key.
senses.whyCN: 生平成为解读作品的钥匙。

senses.title: Biography on screen
senses.definition: a filmed or dramatized account of a life
senses.definitionCN: 以影像呈现的生平记述
senses.example: The channel aired a biography of the explorer.
senses.exampleCN: 频道播出了这位探险家的传记纪录片。
senses.why: Writing-of-a-life transfers to other media.
senses.whyCN: 「书写一生」转移至其他媒介。

senses.title: Collective biographies
senses.definition: works gathering many lives, as national or group biographies
senses.definitionCN: 汇集多人生平的著作，如国家传记辞典
senses.example: The national biography runs to sixty volumes.
senses.exampleCN: 这部国家传记多达六十卷。
senses.why: Many lives bound together keep the same name.
senses.whyCN: 多部小传合订仍沿用此名。

intro.en: Biography joins Greek bios, life, and graphein, to write.
intro.cn: biography 由希腊语 bios「生命」加 graphein「书写」构成。

items.en: gweih₃- meant to live; gwrebh- meant to scratch; reconstructed forms.
items.cn: gweih₃- 意为「活着」；gwrebh- 意为「刻画」（重构形式）。

items.en: bios meant life; graphein meant to write; biographia meant life-writing.
items.cn: 希腊语 bios「生命」、graphein「书写」合成 biographia「为生立传」。

items.en: bios and bioi named the classical genre of lives.
items.cn: 晚期希腊语以 bios 与 bioi 称呼传记文体。

items.en: English biography appears in the 17th century, replacing older word life.
items.cn: 英语 biography 见于 17 世纪，渐代旧词 life。

items.en: now the standard word for life-writing in all media.
items.cn: 如今是各媒介生平书写的标准用语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares bio- or -graphy roots; the near-meaning group gathers life-record words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bio- 或 -graphy 词根；近义组汇集生平记述类词。

entries.definition: the story of one's own life
entries.definitionCN: 自传——auto-（自我）加 biography

entries.definition: a list of books
entries.definitionCN: 参考书目——拼写相近，词根不同

entries.definition: description of the earth
entries.definitionCN: 地理学——共享 -graphy 后缀

entries.definition: a personal record of events the writer knew
entries.definitionCN: 回忆录——亲历视角

entries.definition: the older English word for a biography
entries.definitionCN: 传——英语旧称，如 the life of Johnson

entries.definition: a short characterization of a person
entries.definitionCN: 人物特写——短小而侧写

normalIntro.en: Biography is bio- (life) plus -graphy (writing).
normalIntro.cn: biography 是 bio-（生命）加 -graphy（书写）。

normal.en: Autobiography adds auto-, self.
normal.cn: autobiography 加 auto-（自我）。

normal.en: A biographer writes biographies.
normal.cn: biographer 指传记作者。

normal.en: Bio is the common short form.
normal.cn: bio 是常用缩略。

normal.en: Biographical is the adjective.
normal.cn: 形容词是 biographical。

normal.en: Plutarch's Lives shaped the genre.
normal.cn: 普鲁塔克《名人传》塑造了这一文体。

abstract.en: See a whole life bound under one spine.
abstract.cn: 看一生被装订进一个书脊。

abstract.en: Feel the writer borrowing another's years.
abstract.cn: 感受写作者借走他人岁月。

abstract.en: Picture birth and death as bookends.
abstract.cn: 想象生与死是书立的两端。

examples.en: She spent five years writing the biography of the poet.
examples.cn: 她花五年为诗人立传。

examples.en: Each speaker's biography appeared in the program.
examples.cn: 每位讲者的小传都印在手册里。

examples.en: The film sticks closely to the scientist's biography.
examples.cn: 影片紧贴这位科学家的真实生平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摆哦·格罗菲」——一生事迹摆成一格一格，落笔成传。

root: 希腊语 bios「生命」（上溯至原始印欧语 gweih₃-「活着」，重构形式）加 graphein「书写」（上溯至 gwrebh-「刻画」，重构形式）；biographia 晚期希腊语已用于称传记文体，17 世纪进入英语，取代旧词 life「传」。

sensesIntro.en: The writing of one life spreads into a genre, a sketch, a reading method, and the life itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 「书写一生」扩展为文体、小传、解读法乃至生平本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: another hand tracing one life from first page to last
core.cn: 核心意象：他人之手描摹一个人从首页到末页的一生

branches.en: The written record, long or short
branches.cn: 长传与短传

branches.en: The genre and its traditions
branches.cn: 文体及其传统

branches.en: The life as fact
branches.cn: 作为事实的生平

branches.en: Life as interpretive key
branches.cn: 作为解读钥匙的生平

definition_zh: 小册子作者；写小册子的人
definition_en: a person who writes and distributes short printed arguments, often to attack or defend a cause
core_image: 街角有人把几张纸钉在一起，塞给过路人，纸上满是对当权者的责骂
scene: 那几年他靠印几页纸谋生，骂财政大臣，也骂主教。 For those years he lived by printing a few sheets at a time, attacking the chancellor and the bishops alike, a pamphleteer with ink on his cuffs.
sceneCN: 这里 pamphleteer 指写小册子的人（第 1 个义项：小册子作者）；句意为那几年他靠印几页纸谋生，骂财政大臣也骂主教，是个袖口沾墨的小册子作者。

senses.title: A writer of pamphlets
senses.definition: a person who writes short unbound booklets on a public question
senses.definitionCN: 就公共问题撰写短篇不装订册子的人
senses.example: He lived by printing a few sheets at a time, a pamphleteer with ink on his cuffs.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠一次印几页纸谋生，是个袖口沾墨的小册子作者。
senses.why: The suffix -eer names the person by the thing he makes, like auctioneer and engineer.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -eer 按所造之物来命名人，如 auctioneer 与 engineer。

senses.title: A political writer
senses.definition: a writer whose short works aim at a policy, a party or a minister
senses.definitionCN: 短篇作品针对某项政策、政党或大臣的作者
senses.example: The pamphleteer attacked the chancellor every month.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小册子作者每月攻击财政大臣。
senses.why: Politics gave the word most of its energy and most of its danger.
senses.whyCN: 政治给了这个词大部分能量，也给了它大部分危险。

senses.title: A controversialist
senses.definition: a person who argues in print and prefers a fight to a discussion
senses.definitionCN: 在印刷品中论战、宁可争吵不愿讨论的人
senses.example: He was a pamphleteer first and a thinker second.
senses.exampleCN: 他首先是论战者，其次才是思想家。
senses.why: The word can admire the courage or doubt the depth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以佩服勇气，也可以怀疑深度。

senses.title: A cheap hack writer
senses.definition: a writer paid by the sheet, with more speed than care
senses.definitionCN: 按页取酬、速度多于讲究的写作者
senses.example: The pamphleteer turned out six sheets a week and forgot them all.
senses.exampleCN: 这位写手一周出六页，转眼全忘。
senses.why: Here the trade is visible: pamphlets were cheap and quick.
senses.whyCN: 这里的行业属性露出来了：小册子便宜又快。

senses.title: To write pamphlets
senses.definition: to produce and circulate such sheets, usually for a cause
senses.definitionCN: 制作并散发这类纸页，通常为某项事业
senses.example: He pamphleteered for the cause until the money ran out.
senses.exampleCN: 他为这项事业写小册子，直到钱用完。
senses.why: As a verb the word stresses the activity rather than the person.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，这个词强调活动，而不是人。

senses.title: A seventeenth-century figure
senses.titleCN: 十七世纪的小册子作者
senses.definition: the historical type who fought the civil war with ink and presses
senses.definitionCN: 用墨水与印刷机打内战的历史人物类型
senses.example: Seventeenth-century pamphleteers filled the city with argument.
senses.exampleCN: 十七世纪的小册子作者用论辩填满了这座城市。
senses.why: The word remembers an age when a few pages could change a street.
senses.whyCN: 这个词记得一个几页纸就能改变一条街的时代。

senses.title: A self-appointed campaigner
senses.definition: a person who takes up a public cause without being asked
senses.definitionCN: 未受邀请便承担公共事业的人
senses.example: The pamphleteer had no office and no mandate, only a press.
senses.exampleCN: 这位宣传者没有职位、没有授权，只有一台印刷机。
senses.why: The word is suspicious of self-appointment, even when it admires the result.
senses.whyCN: 这个词对自封总带着疑心，即使它佩服结果。

senses.title: A distributor of sheets
senses.definition: a person who hands the printed sheets to strangers
senses.definitionCN: 把印好的纸页递给陌生人的人
senses.example: The pamphleteer stood at the gate and gave away his argument.
senses.exampleCN: 他站在门口，把自己的论点免费送出。
senses.why: Distribution is half the word: an unread pamphlet changes nothing.
senses.whyCN: 散发是这个词的一半：没人读的小册子什么也改不了。

definition_zh: 客观性；客观态度；客观判断
definition_en: the quality of basing claims on evidence that does not depend on a particular person's feelings, interests or wishes
core_image: 天平两端放相同砝码，指针停在正中，旁边摊着一份任何人都能复核的记录
scene: 评审桌上摆着一架天平，两边砝码相同，指针停在正中，旁边摊着谁都能查的记录。 Objectivity in science means that another team can reach the same result from the same records.
sceneCN: 这里指判断依据可公开复核的证据而不受个人偏好左右（第 1 个义项：判断的客观公正）；句意为科学中的客观性意味着另一支团队凭同样的记录能得出同样的结果。图中可辨识物件：天平、砝码、指针、记录册、评审桌。

pos.zh: 客观性；客观态度；客观判断

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 objectum 经法语而来，义为「对象；反对」
由该名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「客观的；目标」
由客观形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「客观地」
由该名词加表示「使成为」的动词词尾构成，义为「使客观化；物化」
由客观形容词加表示「主义」的词尾构成，义为「客观主义」

senses.title: Impartial judgment based on evidence
senses.definition: the quality of judging by evidence that others can inspect rather than by personal preference
senses.definitionCN: 以他人可核查的证据而非个人偏好来作判断的品质
senses.example: Objectivity in science means that another team can reach the same result from the same records.
senses.exampleCN: 科学中的客观性意味着另一支团队凭同样的记录能得出同样的结果。
senses.why: A judgment is objective when the reasons for it can be shown to someone who does not share the judge's interests.
senses.whyCN: 当判断的理由能展示给一个与判断者利益无关的人时，这个判断才是客观的。

senses.title: Independence from the researcher's bias
senses.definition: the discipline of keeping one's hypotheses, preferences and career interests from deciding what the data are allowed to say
senses.definitionCN: 不让自己的假设、偏好与职业利益决定数据能说什么的自我约束
senses.example: Objectivity does not require the researcher to have no hypothesis, only to test it fairly.
senses.exampleCN: 客观性并不要求研究者没有假设，只要求公平地检验它。
senses.why: The researcher cannot delete expectation, but can arrange the procedure so expectation has no route into the result.
senses.whyCN: 研究者无法删除期待，却可以安排程序，使期待没有路径进入结果。

senses.title: A reality independent of perception
senses.definition: the philosophical claim that objects and facts exist whether or not anyone observes or believes them
senses.definitionCN: 哲学主张：对象与事实是否存在，不取决于是否有人观察或相信
senses.example: The objectivity of the external world is a philosophical claim, not a laboratory finding.
senses.exampleCN: 外部世界的客观性是一个哲学主张，不是实验室的发现。
senses.why: The word begins with something thrown before the mind, and this sense asks whether that thing remains when the mind turns away.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「被抛到心灵之前的东西」开始，这个义项追问心灵转开之后那件东西是否还在。

senses.title: Objective measurement and protocol
senses.definition: the use of defined instruments, fixed procedures and explicit rules so that results do not depend on who happens to run the session
senses.definitionCN: 使用有定义的仪器、固定程序与明确规则，使结果不取决于谁碰巧执行
senses.example: Objective measurement requires that the zero point and the unit be stated in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 客观测量要求零点与单位预先写明。
senses.why: A measurement is objective when the procedure, not the mood of the measurer, fixes the number.
senses.whyCN: 当固定数字的是程序而非测量者的心情时，测量才是客观的。

senses.title: Objectivity in reporting
senses.titleCN: 报道与陈述中的客观性
senses.definition: the separation of verifiable fact from comment, and the attribution of claims to their sources
senses.definitionCN: 把可核实的事实与评论分开，并把说法归到相应来源
senses.example: The editor asked for objectivity in reporting, with every claim attributed.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑要求报道保持客观，每一条说法都要注明来源。
senses.why: A reader who cannot tell fact from comment cannot check either, so the separation is part of public trust.
senses.whyCN: 读者若分不清事实与评论，两者都无法核查，因此这种分离是公共信任的一部分。

senses.title: Fairness in assessment
senses.definition: the application of the same criteria to every case, with reasons that can be stated and reviewed
senses.definitionCN: 对每个个案适用同样标准，并给出可陈述、可复核的理由
senses.example: Objectivity in grading means that two markers reach the same score from the same script.
senses.exampleCN: 评分中的客观性意味着两位评阅人凭同一份答卷给出同样的分数。
senses.why: A grade that cannot be explained by its criteria is a personal verdict wearing the clothes of a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 无法按标准解释的分数，是披着测量外衣的个人裁决。

senses.title: The objectivity of a method
senses.definition: the extent to which a procedure yields the same result across observers, occasions and repetitions
senses.definitionCN: 一种程序在不同观察者、不同场合与重复执行下给出相同结果的程度
senses.example: Inter-rater agreement is one practical test of the objectivity of a coding scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 评分者一致性是检验编码方案客观性的一种实际办法。
senses.why: When a method is objective, the result travels without carrying the name of the person who produced it.
senses.whyCN: 当方法客观时，结果传播时不带着制作者的名字。

senses.title: The critique and the limit
senses.titleCN: 对客观性的批评与限度
senses.definition: the argument that no observer stands outside a perspective, so objectivity must be a discipline of checking rather than a view from nowhere
senses.definitionCN: 主张没有观察者能站在视角之外，因此客观性应是一种核查纪律，而不是「无处之见」
senses.example: The strongest defence of objectivity is procedural: disclose the perspective and invite challenge.
senses.exampleCN: 对客观性最有力的辩护是程序性的：公开视角并接受质疑。
senses.why: If a pure view from nowhere is impossible, objectivity survives as a set of habits that limit the damage of perspective.
senses.whyCN: 如果纯粹的无处之见不可能，客观性就作为一套限制视角损害的习惯而存在。

intro.en: Objectivity comes from Latin objectum, something thrown before the mind, from obicere, to throw against. The abstract noun is modern, built on objective.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 objectum「被抛到心灵之前的东西」，源出 obicere「抛向对面」；抽象名词是近代在 objective 基础上构成的。

items.en: Obicere meant to throw against or place before, from ob- against and iacere to throw.
items.cn: obicere 意为抛向对面或置于面前，由 ob-「对着」与 iacere「抛」构成。

items.en: Objectum named what is placed before the mind, the object of thought rather than the thinker.
items.cn: objectum 指被置于心灵之前的东西，是思想的对象而非思考者。

items.en: Scholastic Latin used objective for what exists in the mind as an object of thought, almost the reverse of the modern sense.
items.cn: 经院拉丁语用 objective 指以思想对象的方式存在，几乎与现代义相反。

items.en: Early modern philosophy reversed the emphasis, and objective came to mean belonging to the object rather than to the mind.
items.cn: 近代早期哲学颠倒重点，objective 转而指属于客体而非心灵。

items.en: The abstract noun objectivity spread in the nineteenth century with science and journalism; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 抽象名词 objectivity 在十九世纪随科学与新闻业传播；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Later thinkers argued that no observer escapes a perspective, which turned objectivity into a discipline of disclosure and checking.
items.cn: 后来的思想家主张没有观察者能摆脱视角，这使客观性变成一种公开与核查的纪律。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like objectivity; the second group names neighbouring ideas of fairness and evidence.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 objectivity 相近；第二组是与「公正、证据」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A thing placed before the mind or before the senses.
entries.definitionCN: 指置于心灵或感官之前的事物。

entries.definition: Belonging to the object rather than to personal feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于客体而非个人感受的。

entries.definition: In a way that can be checked by others.
entries.definitionCN: 指以他人可核查的方式。

entries.definition: To treat something as an object, often with a critical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物当作客体，常带批评意味。

entries.definition: A statement thrown against a claim; it shares the Latin verb but not the sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对某主张提出的反对；共享拉丁动词但词义不同。

entries.definition: Freedom from favouring one side over another.
entries.definitionCN: 指不偏袒任何一方。

entries.definition: Taking no side in a dispute.
entries.definitionCN: 指在争端中不选边。

entries.definition: Treating cases by the same standard.
entries.definitionCN: 指以同一标准对待各个个案。

entries.definition: Consistency of a measure across occasions or raters.
entries.definitionCN: 指测量在不同场合或评分者之间的一致程度。

entries.definition: Emotional distance from the object of study.
entries.definitionCN: 指与研究对象的情绪距离。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Objectum is something thrown before the mind, so objectivity begins with an object rather than a feeling.
normal.cn: objectum 是被抛到心灵之前的东西，因此客观性从客体而非感受开始。

normal.en: Objective and subjectivity are a pair, but they are not two rooms with a wall between; each needs the other to be defined.
normal.cn: 客观性与主观性是一对，但不是隔墙两间房；各自都需要对方才能被定义。

normal.en: A zero point and a unit are the grammar of objective measurement.
normal.cn: 零点与单位是客观测量的语法。

normal.en: Two markers reaching the same score is objectivity made visible.
normal.cn: 两位评阅人给出同一分数，是客观性变得可见。

normal.en: Attribution turns a claim into something a reader can trace.
normal.cn: 注明来源使一个说法变成读者可以追溯的东西。

abstract.en: Objectivity is not the absence of a perspective but the willingness to let the perspective be inspected.
abstract.cn: 客观性不是没有视角，而是愿意让视角接受检查。

abstract.en: The view from nowhere is a useful ideal precisely because no one can stand there.
abstract.cn: 「无处之见」是有用的理想，正因无人能站在那里。

abstract.en: A mirror is objective only until someone forgets to clean it; so is a method.
abstract.cn: 镜子只有在没人忘记擦的时候才客观；方法也是如此。

examples.en: The panel questioned the objectivity of a report funded by the industry it studied.
examples.cn: 评审组质疑一份由被研究行业资助的报告的客观性。

examples.en: Objectivity improves when the raw records are published alongside the conclusion.
examples.cn: 当原始记录与结论一同公布时，客观性会提高。

examples.en: She treated objectivity as a practice of checking, not as a claim of having no perspective.
examples.cn: 她把客观性当作一种核查实践，而不是宣称自己没有视角。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「客体」加「性」——把东西放在天平上，两边砝码一样，谁来看都读同一个数：客观性。

root: 拉丁 obicere「抛向对面」← ob-「对着」+ iacere「抛」，名词 objectum「被置于心灵之前的东西」；近代哲学把重点从心灵转向客体，十九世纪形成抽象名词 objectivity。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from judgment to critique: impartial judgment, independence from researcher bias, an external reality, objective measurement, reporting, fair assessment, the objectivity of methods, and the critique of the ideal itself.
