sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从判断走向反思：公正判断、不受研究者偏差影响、外部实在、客观测量、报道、公平评价、方法客观性，以及对这一理想本身的批评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with equal weights, its pointer resting at the centre, beside a record that anyone may inspect.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架两端砝码相同的天平，指针停在正中，旁边摊着谁都能查的记录。

branches.en: THE FAIR JUDGMENT: the same standard applied to every case, with reasons that can be stated.
branches.cn: 公正判断：对每个个案适用同一标准，并给出可陈述的理由。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE OF THE RESEARCHER: expectation kept out of the route to the result.
branches.cn: 研究者的纪律：不让期待进入结果的通路。

branches.en: THE INDEPENDENT WORLD: facts that remain when the observer turns away.
branches.cn: 独立世界：观察者转开之后仍然存在的事实。

branches.en: THE PROCEDURE AND THE METHOD: fixed instruments, and agreement across observers.
branches.cn: 程序与方法：固定的仪器，以及观察者之间的一致。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC AND THE LIMIT: attributed reporting, and the recognition that no view is from nowhere.
branches.cn: 公开与限度：注明来源的报道，以及承认没有无处之见。

intro.en: Objectivity is a Latin-derived abstract noun built on objective, which descends from objectum.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁来源的抽象名词，建立在「客观的」这一形容词之上，而该形容词又出自 objectum。

latinIntro.en: Latin iacere and obicere supply the throwing before the mind; objectum supplies the noun; -ive and -ity are English endings that turn it into a quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iacere 与 obicere 提供「抛到心灵之前」的动作，objectum 提供名词，形容词词尾与名词词尾把它变成一种性质。

items.example: It places the object before the mind.
items.exampleCN: 它把客体置于心灵之前。

items.example: The oldest image is something thrown.
items.exampleCN: 最早的意象是被抛出的东西。

items.structure: Latin verb from ob- plus iacere
items.example: The verb supplies the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供整个词族。

items.meaning: what is placed before the mind
a thing; an aim; an opposition
items.example: English keeps the thing and the objection together.
items.exampleCN: 英语把「物」与「反对」留在一起。

items.example: The paired word uses the same verb with a different prefix.
items.exampleCN: 配对词用同一动词但前缀不同。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 objectum 经法语而来，义为「对象；反对」
由该名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「客观的；目标」
由客观形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「客观地」
由该名词加表示「使成为」的动词词尾构成，义为「使客观化；物化」
由客观形容词加表示「主义」的词尾构成，义为「客观主义」

definition_zh: 不可逆的；无法挽回的；不可撤销的
definition_en: impossible to turn back, undo or restore to an earlier state
core_image: 推土机把最后一段沙洲推平，河水立刻改了方向，原来的浅滩再也回不来
scene: 河岸边，推土机刚把最后一段沙洲推平，河水立刻改了方向，旧浅滩再也回不来。 Once the wetland was filled, the loss became irreversible.
sceneCN: 这里指已经无法挽回的（第 2 个义项：不可撤销、无法复原）；句意为湿地一旦被填平，损失就再也无法挽回。

pos.zh: 不可逆的；无法挽回的；不可撤销的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示方式的副词尾构成，义为「不可逆地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「不可逆性」
该词去掉否定前缀后的基础形容词，义为「可逆的；可翻转的」

senses.title: Impossible to turn back in direction
senses.definition: of a movement or process that cannot run the opposite way once it has begun
senses.definitionCN: 指运动或过程一旦开始，就无法朝相反方向运行
senses.example: The current through the valve is irreversible, so water never flows back.
senses.exampleCN: 通过阀门的水流不可倒转，所以水从不回流。
senses.why: The base verb means to turn, and the negative prefix forbids the turning back, so the word literally says cannot be turned.
senses.whyCN: 基础动词意为「转」，否定前缀禁止「转回去」，所以这个词字面上就是「不能被转回」。

senses.title: Impossible to undo
senses.definition: of a decision or an act whose effects cannot be cancelled afterwards
senses.definitionCN: 指决定或行为的效果事后无法取消
senses.example: Signing the deed made the sale irreversible.
senses.exampleCN: 签署契据使这笔买卖无法撤销。
senses.why: Some acts are doors that close behind you, and English uses the turning image for exactly those.
senses.whyCN: 有些行为是会在身后关上的门，英语正是用「转回」的意象来形容它们。

senses.title: Of a thermodynamic process
senses.titleCN: 热力学中的不可逆过程
senses.definition: in physics, of a process that increases entropy and cannot be run backwards without outside work
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中指使熵增加、若无外界做功便无法反向进行的过程
senses.example: Heat flowing from a hot body to a cold one is an irreversible process.
senses.exampleCN: 热从高温物体流向低温物体是一个不可逆过程。
senses.why: Physics needed a precise word for the direction of time written into energy, and the everyday word supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 物理学需要为写在能量里的时间方向找一个精确的词，而日常词语正好提供了它。

senses.title: Of permanent damage
senses.definition: of harm to tissue, material or land that no treatment or repair can remove
senses.definitionCN: 指对组织、材料或土地的伤害，任何治疗或修复都无法消除
senses.example: The frost caused irreversible damage to the young trees.
senses.exampleCN: 霜冻对幼树造成了不可逆的损伤。
senses.why: Damage is measured by whether it can be repaired, and this word marks the point where repair stops being possible.
senses.whyCN: 损伤以能否修复来衡量，而这个词标出了修复不再可能的那条线。

senses.title: Of a change that cannot be reversed
senses.definition: of a long trend or transformation that will not return to its starting condition
senses.definitionCN: 指长期趋势或转变不会回到起始状态
senses.example: The shift from coal to gas proved irreversible.
senses.exampleCN: 从煤转向天然气的转变被证明不可逆转。
senses.why: Large changes are judged by whether a society could plausibly go back, and the word answers that question.
senses.whyCN: 重大变化以「社会是否可能退回」来评判，而这个词回答的正是这个问题。

senses.title: Of a medical condition
senses.definition: of a disease or loss of function that treatment can slow but never restore
senses.definitionCN: 指治疗只能延缓、永远无法恢复的疾病或功能丧失
senses.example: The scan showed irreversible damage to the optic nerve.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示视神经受到了不可逆的损伤。
senses.why: Medicine divides conditions by whether the body can return, and the word names the side where it cannot.
senses.whyCN: 医学以身体能否恢复来划分病情，而这个词命名的正是「不能」的那一侧。

senses.title: Of a commitment that cannot be withdrawn
senses.definition: of a promise or contract that binds the maker with no way out
senses.definitionCN: 指承诺或合同约束作出者，没有退路
senses.example: The treaty created an irreversible commitment to the alliance.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约造成了对同盟不可撤回的承诺。
senses.why: A promise is a door that locks, and the turning image suits a choice that cannot be taken back.
senses.whyCN: 承诺是一扇会锁上的门，「转回」的意象正适合无法收回的选择。

senses.title: Of an environmental loss
senses.definition: of the destruction of an ecosystem or species that no restoration can bring back
senses.definitionCN: 指生态系统或物种的毁坏，任何修复都无法带回
senses.example: Draining the marsh caused an irreversible loss of habitat.
senses.exampleCN: 排干沼泽造成了栖息地的不可逆丧失。
senses.why: Extinction is the clearest case of no return, and the word carries that finality into policy language.
senses.whyCN: 灭绝是「无法回头」最清楚的例子，而这个词把这种终结性带进政策语言。

senses.title: Of decline that cannot be halted
senses.definition: of a fall in health, memory or capacity that continues regardless of effort
senses.definitionCN: 指健康、记忆或能力的下降，无论怎样努力都持续下去
senses.example: The patient entered an irreversible decline after the second stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次中风之后，病人进入了不可逆转的衰退。
senses.why: Decline is a slope, and a slope with no uphill direction is naturally called irreversible.
senses.whyCN: 衰退是一道坡，而没有上坡方向的坡自然被称作不可逆。

intro.en: Irreversible joins a negative prefix to reversible, which comes from Latin reversibilis, from revertere, to turn back, built from re-, back, and vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: 这个词把否定前缀加在 reversible 上，而 reversible 出自拉丁语 reversibilis，来自 revertere「转回」，由 re-「向后」与 vertere「转」构成。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, and its family reaches English through convert, divert, invert and version.
items.cn: vertere 意为转，其同族通过 convert、divert、invert 与 version 进入英语。

items.en: The compound meant to turn back or return, and it is the direct ancestor of reverse and revert.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为转回、返回，是 reverse 与 revert 的直接祖先。

items.en: The adjective meant able to be turned back, a word of logic and later of physics.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「可以被转回的」，先是逻辑学术语，后来成为物理学术语。

items.en: French passed the adjective to English, where reversible described garments, decisions and machines.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词传给英语，reversible 在那里形容可翻面的衣物、可撤销的决定与可反转的机器。

items.en: English formed the negative with the assimilated prefix ir-, and the word entered technical writing in the nineteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用同化后的前缀 ir- 构成否定形式，这个词在十九世纪进入技术写作；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Thermodynamics gave the word its sharpest sense, where an irreversible process fixes the direction of time.
items.cn: 热力学赋予这个词最锋利的意义：不可逆过程固定了时间的方向。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like irreversible; the second group names neighbouring ideas of permanence.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 irreversible 相近；第二组是与「永久、不可更改」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Able to be turned back or undone, the base of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以转回或撤销的，是本词的基础形式。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a way that cannot be undone.
entries.definitionCN: 指以无法挽回的方式。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being impossible to reverse.
entries.definitionCN: 指不可逆转状态的名词。

entries.definition: To turn something the other way, or the opposite side of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物转向另一面，或指其反面。

entries.definition: Impossible to cancel; it looks close but its root means to call back, not to turn.
entries.definitionCN: 指无法取消的；形近，但词根意为「召回」而非「转」。

entries.definition: Lasting for the whole future, with no planned end.
entries.definitionCN: 指持续到整个未来，没有计划的终点。

entries.definition: Of damage or loss that cannot be repaired or made good.
entries.definitionCN: 指损伤或损失无法修复或弥补。

entries.definition: Of something that cannot be recovered once lost.
entries.definitionCN: 指一旦失去便无法找回。

entries.definition: Settling a matter so that no further change is allowed.
entries.definitionCN: 指对事情作出定论，不再允许更改。

entries.definition: Of a bad condition that no remedy can cure.
entries.definitionCN: 指恶劣状况无药可救。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the negative prefix, the turning root and the scientific phrases the word now lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用否定前缀、「转」的词根，以及这个词如今栖身的科学搭配。

normal.en: Reverse means to turn back, so irreversible means the turning back is forbidden.
normal.cn: 同族动词意为「转回」，所以这个词意为「转回被禁止」。

normal.en: The same root builds convert, divert and invert, all of which describe a change of direction.
normal.cn: 同一词根构成表示「转换」「转向」与「倒转」的同族词，都在描述方向的改变。

normal.en: An irreversible process is the physicist's way of saying time has a direction.
normal.cn: 不可逆过程是物理学家表达「时间有方向」的方式。

normal.en: Irreversible damage is the phrase used in medicine, law and environmental reports alike.
normal.cn: 不可逆损伤是医学、法律与环境报告中都在用的说法。

normal.en: The prefix appears as ir- rather than in- because the following sound is r.
normal.cn: 否定前缀在流音前发生同化，拼写也随之改变。

abstract.en: Irreversible is the price tag attached to any act that closes its own door.
abstract.cn: 「不可逆」是贴在一切自我关门的行为上的价签。

abstract.en: The word does not say the past is long; it says the past cannot be re-entered.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的不是过去很长，而是过去无法再进入。

abstract.en: Every irreversible choice makes the future narrower and the present heavier.
abstract.cn: 每一个不可逆的选择都让未来更窄、当下更重。

examples.en: Once the ice sheet melts past that point, the rise becomes irreversible.
examples.cn: 一旦冰盖越过那个临界点，海面上升就变得不可逆。

examples.en: The court treated the transfer of land as an irreversible act.
examples.cn: 法院把这块土地的转让视为不可撤销的行为。

examples.en: Years of overgrazing pushed the grassland into irreversible decline.
examples.cn: 多年过度放牧把草原推入不可逆转的衰退。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「伊利佛瑟波」——「伊利」都「佛」了，倒带键按不下去：不可逆的

root: 拉丁语 reversibilis「可转回的」← revertere「转回」← re-「向后」+ vertere「转」；英语加同化否定前缀 ir- 构成。vertere 同族有 convert、divert、invert、version。十九世纪进入技术写作，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses apply one idea to different fields: direction, undone acts, entropy, damage, trends, illness, promises, extinction and decline.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把同一个观念用到不同领域：方向、撤销的行为、熵、损伤、趋势、疾病、承诺、物种灭绝与衰退。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river that has cut a new channel and will not return to the old one.
core.cn: 核心意象：河流已开出新河道，不会回到旧河道。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL DIRECTION BRANCH: flow that cannot run backwards and entropy that only grows.
branches.cn: 物理方向分支：不能倒流的水流，以及只增不减的熵。

branches.en: THE BINDING ACT BRANCH: a signature or a promise that closes behind the maker.
branches.cn: 约束行为分支：在作出者身后关上的签字或承诺。

branches.en: THE BODY AND MATERIAL BRANCH: damage that no treatment or repair can remove.
branches.cn: 身体与材料分支：任何治疗或修复都无法消除的损伤。

branches.en: THE LARGE-SCALE BRANCH: social trends and lost habitats that will not return.
branches.cn: 大规模分支：不会回返的社会趋势与消失的栖息地。

branches.en: THE SLOPE BRANCH: decline with no uphill direction left.
branches.cn: 斜坡分支：没有上坡方向可走的衰退。

intro.en: Irreversible is a Latin adjective of turning with a negative prefix that has assimilated to the following sound.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「转」的拉丁形容词，加上一个已与后接音同化的否定前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vertere, revertere and reversibilis; the English negative prefix appears as ir- before r.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 vertere、revertere 与 reversibilis；英语否定前缀在 r 前写作 ir-。

items.example: The prefix marks a return to the starting point.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出回到起点。

items.example: The root builds many English direction words.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根构成许多英语方向词。

items.example: The compound is the source of reverse.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是表示「逆转」的同族词的来源。
它构成表示「不可逆性」的名词。
它构成表示「不可逆地」的副词。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示方式的副词尾构成，义为「不可逆地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「不可逆性」
该词去掉否定前缀后的基础形容词，义为「可逆的；可翻转的」

definition_zh: 政党；政党组织；选举中的竞争方；执政党或在野党
definition_en: an organized group of people who share political aims and compete in elections to win power
core_image: 一间挂满标语的办公室，几个人围着名单分工，把散开的意见拧成一支能推上选举台的队伍
scene: 总部墙上贴满各区联络人的名单，志愿者按门牌分片，把零散的支持登记成册。 The political party opened a branch office in every district before the election.
sceneCN: 总部墙上贴满各区联络人的名单，志愿者按门牌分片，把零散的支持登记成册；句中的这个说法指「围绕共同主张组织起来、通过选举争取权力的团体」（第 1 个义项：以取得执政地位为目标的正式组织）。图中可辨识物件：标语、分区地图、登记册、门牌、折叠桌。

senses.title: Organized group seeking power
senses.titleCN: 以争取执政为目标的正式组织
senses.definition: a formally organized group of people who share aims and compete for public office
senses.definitionCN: 由一批主张相同的人正式组织起来、为取得公职而竞争的团体
senses.example: Every political party must publish its accounts each year.
senses.exampleCN: 每个政党每年都必须公布自己的账目。
senses.why: The compound joins 'of the city' with 'part': a section of the citizen body organizes itself and aims at the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法把「城邦的」和「部分」拼在一起：公民整体中的一部分组织起来，目标却指向整个城邦。

senses.title: The party apparatus
senses.definition: the offices, staff and branches that keep a party running between elections
senses.definitionCN: 在两次选举之间维持政党运转的办公室、工作人员与地方分支
senses.example: The party apparatus was rebuilt from the local branches upward.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党的组织机构从地方分支开始逐层重建。
senses.why: A party is not only a label on a ballot; it is also a building, a payroll and a filing system.
senses.whyCN: 政党不只是选票上的一个名字，它还是一栋楼、一份工资单和一套档案。

senses.title: Competitor in an election
senses.definition: one of the organized sides that voters choose between at the polls
senses.definitionCN: 投票时供选民在其中择一的组织化一方
senses.example: Five political parties contested the same seat.
senses.exampleCN: 五个政党争夺同一个席位。
senses.why: Elections reduce many opinions to a short list of named sides, and each side is a party.
senses.whyCN: 选举把众多意见压缩成一份短短的名单，名单上的每一方就是一个政党。

senses.title: The parliamentary group
senses.definition: the members of one party sitting together in a legislature and voting as a bloc
senses.definitionCN: 同一政党的议员在立法机构中坐在一起、作为一个整体投票
senses.example: The party held a caucus meeting before the final vote.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党在最终投票前召开了党团会议。
senses.why: Once inside the chamber, the electoral side becomes a working group with whips and a common line.
senses.whyCN: 进入议事厅之后，选举中的一方就变成一个配有督导、持有统一立场的运作团体。

senses.title: The governing party
senses.definition: the party that holds office and directs the government after an election
senses.definitionCN: 选举后掌握职位、领导政府的那一个政党
senses.example: The governing party lost three ministers in a single week.
senses.exampleCN: 执政党在一周之内失去了三名部长。
senses.why: Winning turns the competitor into the office-holder; the same organization now answers for the state.
senses.whyCN: 获胜把竞争方变成掌权方；同一个组织从此要为整个国家作答。

senses.title: The party out of office
senses.definition: a party that does not hold government and watches the office-holders from outside
senses.definitionCN: 不掌握政府、从外部盯住掌权者的政党
senses.example: The party out of office pressed for a public inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 在野的那个政党极力主张进行公开调查。
senses.why: The compound is neutral, so the same words describe the winner and the watcher; only the seat of power decides which.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法本身是中性的，同一串字既能指赢家也能指旁观者，只看权力坐在哪一边。

senses.title: Membership and affiliation
senses.definition: the status of belonging to a party, with dues, rights and a shared label
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个政党的身份，附带党费、权利与共同的名号
senses.example: Her party membership dates from her student years.
senses.exampleCN: 她的党员身份始于学生时代。
senses.why: The organization exists only while people carry cards, pay dues and call themselves members.
senses.whyCN: 组织之所以存在，是因为有人持证、缴费并自称成员。

senses.title: Historical party types
senses.titleCN: 群众党与干部党等历史类型
senses.definition: kinds of party defined by how they recruit: mass membership or a small professional core
senses.definitionCN: 按招募方式划分的政党类型：广泛吸收党员的群众党，或人数精简的职业核心
senses.example: Historians contrast the mass party with the older cadre party.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学者把群众党与更早的干部党放在一起对照。
senses.why: As suffrage widened, parties had to choose between enrolling millions and relying on a few professionals.
senses.whyCN: 随着选举权扩大，政党必须在两条路之间选择：吸收数百万人，或依靠少数专业人士。

intro.en: The adjective goes back to Greek polis 'city-state' through politikos 'of the city'; the noun goes through Old French to Latin pars 'part'. When the two were fixed as one label is not securely dated, so the first use is best treated as uncertain.
intro.cn: 形容词部分出自希腊语中意为「城邦」的词，经意为「城邦的、公民的」形容词进入英语；名词部分经古法语上溯到拉丁语中意为「部分」的词。两者何时固定成一个说法，首见年代无法确证，只能存疑。

items.en: Polis named the self-governing city and its citizen body. The word is Greek, not Latin, and it supplies the idea of public affairs rather than of a private household.
items.cn: 这个希腊语词指自治城邦及其公民全体。它提供的是公共事务的观念，与私人家庭相对。

items.en: Politikos meant 'of the city, of a citizen'. Latin borrowed it as politicus, and English political descends from that line.
items.cn: 这个希腊语形容词意为「城邦的、公民的」。拉丁语借入后，英语的形容词就出自这一条线。

items.en: Pars, genitive partis, meant 'part, portion, share'. The accusative partem sits behind the French and English forms.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语名词意为「部分、份、份额」，它的宾格形式是法语与英语形式的来源。

items.en: Partie meant 'part, portion, side', and also the act of dividing. English took it as party, first meaning a part or a side.
items.cn: 这个古法语词意为「部分、份、一方」，也指分割的动作。英语借入后，最初表示「部分」或「一方」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century party could mean a faction or a side in a quarrel. The date when it settled into 'organized political group' is generally placed in the eighteenth century but is not exact.
items.cn: 这个名词到十七世纪已可指派系或争执中的一方。它固定为「有组织的政治团体」的时间，一般认为在十八世纪，但无法精确。

items.en: Political party became a standard label as elections widened in the nineteenth century. Earlier writers used party alone, and the compound's first appearance remains uncertain.
items.cn: 到十九世纪选举范围扩大，这个由两部分组成的说法才成为标准称谓。更早的作者单用后半段，组合形式首见于何时仍不确定。

note.en: The first group shares a spelling stem or a Latin source; the second group holds things that come close in meaning without being the same institution.
note.cn: 第一组共享拼写词干或拉丁来源；第二组是意思接近、但并非同一种制度的说法。

entries.definition: On its own it can mean a social gathering or one side in a dispute as well as a political group. The compound narrows it to the organized body.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时，它既可指社交聚会或争执中的一方，也可指政治团体；加上前面的形容词后，只保留有组织团体这一层。

entries.definition: A portion, a piece or a role. It shares the Latin source with party but never means an organization of people.
entries.definitionCN: 指一部分、一个零件或一个角色。它与前面的名词同出拉丁来源，但从不表示人的组织。

entries.definition: A devoted supporter of a side, often one who will not listen to the other side. It names a person or an attitude, not the institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一方的坚定支持者，往往不肯听另一方的话。它指人或态度，不指制度本身。

entries.definition: The activity of governing and competing for power. It is the field in which a party works, not the party itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指治理与争夺权力的活动，是政党在其中运作的领域，而不是政党本身。

entries.definition: A smaller group within a larger body, often held together by one interest. It is usually narrower and more quarrelsome than a party.
entries.definitionCN: 较大团体内部的小团体，常由某一项利益维系。它通常比政党更窄，也更好斗。

entries.definition: A loose campaign around a cause. It may support candidates but need not contest elections as an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕某项事业形成的松散运动。它可以支持候选人，却不必作为组织参加选举。

entries.definition: A group of states or members acting together for voting strength. It is defined by joint action, not by a membership card.
entries.definitionCN: 为投票力量而共同行动的一群国家或成员。它靠联合行动界定，而不靠党员证。

entries.definition: An alliance of parties formed for a purpose and able to dissolve. A party is a lasting organization; a coalition is a deal between such organizations.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目的结成的政党联盟，可以解散。政党是持久组织，联盟则是这类组织之间的交易。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek city-state behind the adjective, the Latin 'part' behind the noun, real derived words and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：形容词背后是希腊城邦，名词背后是拉丁语「部分」，再加上真实派生词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Polis 'city-state' gives the adjective: a party deals in public affairs, not private ones.
normal.cn: 希腊语中意为「城邦」的词给出形容词部分：政党处理的是公共事务，不是私事。

normal.en: Pars 'part' gives the noun: a party is one part of the citizen body organized for the whole.
normal.cn: 拉丁语中意为「部分」的词给出名词部分：政党是公民整体中被组织起来的那一部分。

normal.en: The family runs politics, politician, political, politically and partisan.
normal.cn: 同族词包括政治、政治家、政治的、政治上与党派支持者这几个词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the institution: join a political party, form a political party, the ruling political party.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这一制度：加入政党、组建政党、执政党。

normal.en: Its mirror image is the party out of office, which watches rather than governs.
normal.cn: 它的镜像是在野的那个政党，只监督而不执政。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd splitting into two rows of chairs, then each row choosing a name and a colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人分成两排椅子，然后每一排给自己取一个名字、挑一种颜色。

abstract.en: A party is a part that behaves as if it were the whole, until the next vote corrects it.
abstract.cn: 政党就是一部分人表现得仿佛自己是整体，直到下一次投票把它纠正过来。

abstract.en: The label on the ballot is the visible tip; the offices and dues are the body underneath.
abstract.cn: 选票上的名字只是露出的尖端，底下的办公室与党费才是它的身体。

examples.en: A political party that cannot raise funds cannot print a single poster.
examples.cn: 一个筹不到钱的政党连一张海报都印不出来。

examples.en: The same political party has governed the country for three terms.
examples.cn: 同一个政党已经连续三次执政。

examples.en: Local members of the political party met in a rented hall to choose a candidate.
examples.cn: 这个政党的本地党员在一间租来的礼堂里开会，挑选候选人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡里提扣·帕提」——先「破立」旧规矩，再「替」人办事，最后「怕踢」出局，正好是一支争权的队伍

root: 希腊语 polis「城邦」经 politikos「城邦的、公民的」进入英语作形容词；名词部分经古法语上溯到拉丁 pars/partem「部分、份」，本义「一部分人」，后固定指政党。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one body through time: a part of the citizens organizes, competes, sits, governs, watches itself and finally takes different historical shapes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个团体走完一圈：公民中的一部分先组织起来，再参加竞争、进入议事厅、掌握政府、从外部盯住自己，最后分化出不同的历史形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a part of the citizens turns itself into a named body and aims at the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：公民中的一部分把自己变成一个有名字的团体，并把目标指向整体。

branches.en: FORM AND VARIETY: the basic organized group and the historical shapes it takes when recruiting members.
branches.cn: 形态与变体：基本的有组织团体，以及它在招募成员时分化出的历史形态。

branches.en: BODY AND MEMBERS: offices and staff keep it running, while cards and dues keep it populated.
branches.cn: 躯体与成员：办公室和职员让它运转，党员证与党费让它有人。

branches.en: OUTSIDE AND INSIDE: on the ballot it is a competitor, inside the chamber it is a voting bloc.
branches.cn: 门外与门内：在选票上它是竞争方，进了议事厅它就是一个投票集团。

branches.en: IN OFFICE: winning converts the competitor into the body that answers for the state.
branches.cn: 掌权：胜选把竞争方变成替国家作答的机构。

branches.en: OUT OF OFFICE: the same label now marks the watcher rather than the office-holder.
branches.cn: 在野：同一个名号现在标的是旁观者，而不是掌权者。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Greek-derived adjective with a French-derived noun, and each part has its own family of suffixes and related words.
intro.cn: 这个短语由希腊来源的形容词与法语来源的名词拼成，两部分各自带一串后缀与相关词。

latinIntro.en: Greek polis supplies the first element through politikos; Latin pars, partis supplies the second through Old French. Latin politicus is a later borrowing of the Greek adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 第一段来自希腊语中意为「城邦」的词；第二段来自拉丁语中意为「部分」的名词，经古法语进入英语。后来拉丁语又借入了那个希腊形容词。

items.structure: politic- (Greek polis 'city-state' via politikos) + -al (Latin adjective suffix)
items.meaning: of the city, of public affairs
items.meaningCN: 城邦的；公共事务的，语义偏移为「政治的」
items.example: The debate turned political within minutes.
items.exampleCN: 辩论几分钟内就变成了政治争论。

items.structure: politic- + -s (Greek plural ta politika 'affairs of the city')
items.meaningCN: 公共事务的领域，由形容词转为学科与活动之名

items.meaning: one who works in public affairs
items.meaningCN: 从事公共事务的人，语义偏移为「政治家、政客」

items.structure: part- (Latin pars, partem 'part') + -y (noun suffix through Old French -ie)
items.meaningCN: 部分或一方，语义偏移为「政党、聚会」
items.example: The party chose a new leader.

items.structure: part- + -isan (adherent suffix through French and Italian)
items.meaning: a devoted follower of a side
items.meaningCN: 某一方的忠实跟随者，语义偏移为「党徒、偏袒的」
items.exampleCN: 党派性的欢呼声淹没了提问。

items.meaning: of a part only; hence biased
items.meaningCN: 只涉及一部分的，语义偏移为「不完整的、偏袒的」
items.example: The report was partial and incomplete.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告既偏袒又不完整。

items.meaningCN: 取一份，语义偏移为「参与、分享」
items.example: Guests may partake of the buffet.

items.meaning: the state of sharing an enterprise
items.meaningCN: 合伙关系，语义偏移为「伙伴关系、合伙企业」
items.example: The two firms signed a partnership.
items.exampleCN: 这两家公司签署了合伙协议。

definition_zh: 防御；保卫；防御工事；辩护；防守
definition_en: the act of protecting someone or something against attack, or the means used to do so
core_image: 一道石墙横在城门之前，墙上站着持盾的守兵
scene: 山口的城堡没有护城河，只有一道厚墙挡在骑兵必经之路上。 The castle's outer wall was built as a first line of defense against cavalry.
sceneCN: 这里 defense 指「抵御进攻的军事防御」（第 1 个义项：以工事或兵力阻止敌方推进）；句意为这座城堡的外墙被建成抵御骑兵的第一道防线。图中可辨识物件：石墙、城门、持盾守兵、远处骑兵。

pos.zh: 防御；保卫；防御工事；辩护；防守（美式拼写；英式拼作 defence）

senses.title: Military protection against attack
senses.definition: the organised resistance of armed forces or fortifications against an enemy
senses.definitionCN: 武装力量或工事对敌方进攻的有组织抵抗
senses.example: The castle's outer wall was built as a first line of defense against cavalry.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城堡的外墙被建成抵御骑兵的第一道防线。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to ward off'; the noun names the whole activity of warding off.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「挡开」；名词命名整个挡开的活动。

senses.title: Legal defence of a case
senses.definition: the argument and evidence presented to protect a person or position in a legal proceeding
senses.definitionCN: 在法律程序中为保护某人或某立场而提出的论证与证据
senses.example: The lawyer mounted a strong defense of the client's innocence.
senses.exampleCN: 律师为当事人的清白作了有力的辩护。
senses.why: A trial is an attack on a claim, and answering it is the same act of warding off.
senses.whyCN: 审判是对某项主张的攻击，回应它就是同一种挡开行为。

senses.title: Defensive play in sport
senses.definition: the part of a game in which a team tries to stop the opponent from scoring
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中一方力图阻止对手得分的那一部分
senses.example: Their defense held for the final ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的防守在最后十分钟守住了。
senses.why: Sport reuses the military frame: one side attacks, the other wards off.
senses.whyCN: 体育沿用军事框架：一方进攻，另一方挡开。

senses.title: Biological immune defence
senses.definition: the body's systems for resisting infection or damage
senses.definitionCN: 身体抵抗感染或损伤的系统
senses.example: The skin is the body's first defense against infection.
senses.exampleCN: 皮肤是身体抵抗感染的第一道防御。
senses.why: The body treats infection as an attack, so the military noun fits without metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 身体把感染当作进攻，军事名词无需比喻便适用。

senses.title: Self-defence against physical harm
senses.definition: action taken to protect oneself from immediate physical danger
senses.definitionCN: 为保护自己免受即时人身危险而采取的行动
senses.example: She took a self-defense class before moving to the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她在搬到大城市前上了一门自卫课。
senses.why: Self-defence narrows the object of protection to one's own body.
senses.whyCN: 自卫把保护对象收窄到自己的身体。

senses.title: Verbal justification of an idea
senses.definition: a spoken or written argument in support of a person, policy or belief
senses.definitionCN: 为某人、某政策或某信念作支持的口头或书面论证
senses.example: He wrote a defense of the new tax in the newspaper.
senses.exampleCN: 他在报纸上写了一篇为新税辩护的文章。
senses.why: A claim can be attacked, and answering it repeats the same warding-off.
senses.whyCN: 主张可以被攻击，回应它就是同一种挡开。

senses.title: A fortification or barrier
senses.definition: a concrete structure such as a wall, ditch or bunker built to stop an attack
senses.definitionCN: 为阻止进攻而建的墙、壕沟或掩体等实体结构
senses.example: The old defense crumbled after two centuries of rain.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧防御工事在两百年雨水侵蚀后坍塌了。
senses.why: The abstract act hardens into a concrete wall.
senses.whyCN: 抽象行为凝固成具体的墙。

senses.title: Psychological defence
senses.definition: an unconscious mental strategy that protects a person from anxiety or painful insight
senses.definitionCN: 保护个人免于焦虑或痛苦觉察的无意识心理策略
senses.example: Humor can serve as a defense against bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 幽默可以作为面对坏消息的一种防御。
senses.why: What cannot be stopped outside can be kept outside the mind.
senses.whyCN: 外部挡不住的东西，可以挡在心灵之外。

intro.en: Defense comes from Latin defensa, the feminine of defensus, past participle of defendere 'to ward off'. The verb joins de- 'away' to fendere 'to strike'. English uses defense in American spelling and defence in British.
intro.cn: defense 来自拉丁 defensa，即 defendere「挡开」的过去分词 defensus 的阴性形式。该动词由 de-「离开」与 fendere「击打」构成。英语美式拼作 defense，英式拼作 defence。

items.en: Defendere meant 'to ward off, repel, protect' and is the source of defend, defense and defensive.
items.cn: defendere 意为「挡开、击退、保护」，是 defend、defense 与 defensive 的来源。

items.en: The prefix de- here carries the sense 'away, off', giving the compound the idea of driving something off.
items.cn: 前缀 de- 在此表示「离开、推开」，使复合词带有「把某物赶开」的意思。

items.en: Fendere 'to strike' is rare outside compounds; it also lies behind offend and fend.
items.cn: fendere「击打」很少单独出现，只见于复合词；offend 与 fend 也出自它。

items.en: Old French defense carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in the military sense.
items.cn: 古法语 defense 于 14 世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初为军事义。

items.en: British English kept defence from the French form, while American English standardized defense after Webster.
items.cn: 英式英语保留法语形式的 defence，美式英语则在韦伯斯特之后统一为 defense。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): fendere is poorly attested outside compounds, and its deeper origin is reconstructed rather than recorded; the first English date is approximate. The defendere layer is secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：fendere 在复合词之外少有记录，其更早来源属重构而非有记录的形式；英语首见年代为约数；defendere 这一层可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the noun from its spelling variant and its family members; group two separates kinds of protection by means and by setting.
note.cn: 第一组区分该名词与拼写变体、同族成员；第二组按手段与场景区分各类保护。

entries.definition: The same noun in British spelling; American texts write defense.
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词的英式拼写；美式文本写 defense。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a posture or attitude; it cannot stand for the noun itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述姿态或态度的形容词；不能代替名词本身。

entries.definition: A person who defends; it is an agent noun, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行保卫的人；是施动名词，不是行为。

entries.definition: Able to be justified or held; it judges the case rather than naming the defence.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被辩护或可守住的；评价该主张，而非命名防御。

entries.definition: Keeping something safe from any harm; defense usually implies a specific attack to be warded off.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物免受任何伤害；defense 通常暗示有具体进攻需要挡开。

entries.definition: The act of opposing a force; defense is the broader plan of which resistance may be one part.
entries.definitionCN: 指对抗某种力量的行为；defense 是更宏大的方案，抵抗可以是其中一环。

entries.definition: A watch kept to prevent surprise; defense can be static or active and need not involve watching.
entries.definitionCN: 指为防止突袭而进行的警戒；defense 可以是静态或主动的，不一定涉及警戒。

entries.definition: The giving of reasons; a legal defense is a structured argument, while justification is the general act.
entries.definitionCN: 指给出理由；法律上的 defense 是有结构的论证，而 justification 是一般行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb of warding off, the real spelling split, and the collocations that mark each sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「挡开」动词、真实的拼写分歧，以及标记各义项的固定搭配。

normal.en: de- 'away' + fendere 'strike': strike the attack away.
normal.cn: de-「离开」+ fendere「击打」：把进攻打开。

normal.en: The family runs defend, defense, defensive, defender, defensible.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 defend、defense、defensive、defender、defensible。

normal.en: American defense, British defence.
normal.cn: 美式 defense，英式 defence。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: national defense, self-defense, in defense of.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 national defense、self-defense、in defense of。

normal.en: Five arenas: army, court, field, body, mind.
normal.cn: 五个场域：军队、法庭、赛场、身体、心理。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that exists only because someone once charged at it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道墙，它的存在只因为曾有人冲向它。

abstract.en: Picture a lawyer's sentence standing where a shield would stand.
abstract.cn: 想象律师的一句话立在盾牌本该立的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a joke raised like a small shield in front of bad news.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑话像小盾牌一样举在坏消息之前。

examples.en: The ministry spends more on defense than on education.
examples.cn: 该部在国防上的开支超过教育。

examples.en: The court heard the defense's final argument.
examples.cn: 法庭听取了辩护方的最后陈述。

examples.en: A strong defense kept the score level until the last minute.
examples.cn: 稳固的防守把比分保持到最后时刻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「de（离开）+ fense（打）」——把进攻打开 → 防御；保卫

root: 拉丁 de-「离开」+ fendere「击打」→ defendere「挡开」→ 过去分词 defensus → 名词 defensa → 英语 defense；fendere 更早来源为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one wall: an army holds a line, a lawyer holds a case, a team holds a score, a body holds off infection, and a mind holds off anxiety.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一道墙：军队守住一线，律师守住一案，球队守住比分，身体挡住感染，心理挡住焦虑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick wall standing between a gate and the cavalry on the road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道厚墙立在城门与路上的骑兵之间。

branches.en: PHYSICAL WALL: troops and fortifications stop a moving enemy.
branches.cn: 实体墙：兵力与工事挡住推进的敌军。

branches.en: VERBAL WALL: argument answers an attack on a claim or policy.
branches.cn: 言语墙：论证回应针对主张或政策的攻击。

branches.en: PERSONAL WALL: a player or a person guards a score or a body.
branches.cn: 个人墙：球员守住比分，个人守住身体。

branches.en: BIOLOGICAL WALL: skin and immunity resist infection.
branches.cn: 生物墙：皮肤与免疫抵抗感染。

branches.en: MENTAL WALL: humour and other strategies keep anxiety at a distance.
branches.cn: 心理墙：幽默等策略把焦虑挡在远处。

intro.en: Defense is a Latin participle turned noun; the family adds agent, adjective and negative suffixes to the same defendere stem.
intro.cn: defense 是由拉丁分词转成的名词；该词族在同一 defendere 词干上加施动、形容词与否定后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin defendere, defensio and fendere supply the stem, the action noun and the rare verb of striking.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 defendere、defensio 与 fendere 提供词干、动作名词与罕见的「击打」动词。

items.example: The unit defended the bridge for a week.
items.exampleCN: 这支部队守了那座桥一周。

items.meaning: the act or means of warding off
items.example: The defense held through the night.
They took a defensive position on the hill.
items.exampleCN: 他们在山上占据防御位置。

items.meaning: able to be justified or held
items.example: The claim is defensible but thin.
items.exampleCN: 这一主张可辩护，但根基薄弱。

items.example: The nestlings are defenseless for weeks.
items.exampleCN: 雏鸟在数周内毫无防备。
她是出于自卫才行动的。

items.example: The defense line ran along the river.

definition_zh: 大主教；总主教
definition_en: a bishop of the highest rank who is in charge of all the churches in a large area or country
core_image: 教堂塔尖下披深红法衣、统管一省众主教的高级神职者
scene: 加冕典礼上，钟声齐鸣，众人起立。 The archbishop placed the crown on the new king's head.
sceneCN: 这里 archbishop 是「大主教」（第 1 个义项：最高级别的主教）；句意是大主教为新国王加冕。

collocations.zh: 坎特伯雷大主教（英格兰圣公会首领）

collocations.phrase: under the authority of the archbishop

derivatives.zh: 主教，archbishop 由 bishop 加前缀构成
bishop 加 -ric（管辖区域）后缀，义为「大主教的辖区或职位」
与希腊词根 episkopos 同源，义为「主教的」
archbishop 的形容词形式，义为「大主教的」

senses.title: A bishop of the highest rank
senses.definition: a Christian bishop who supervises other bishops and leads the church in a province or country
senses.definitionCN: 统辖其他主教、领导一个大区或国家教会的最高级主教
senses.example: The archbishop called a meeting of all the bishops in the province.
senses.exampleCN: 大主教召集了全省的主教开会。
senses.why: The prefix arch- means chief, so the word literally means chief bishop.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 arch- 表示「首要的」，字面即「主教之首」，故引出统辖众主教的大主教义。

senses.title: A senior religious authority in metaphorical use
senses.definition: a person regarded as the leading authority in a field, by extension of the church sense
senses.definitionCN: 由教会义延伸，指被视为某一领域最高权威的人物
senses.example: Journalists called him the archbishop of modern architecture criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们称他为现代建筑批评的最高权威。
senses.why: Because an archbishop stands at the top of a hierarchy, the title transfers to any supreme authority.
senses.whyCN: 大主教居于等级制顶端，这一形象便转移到任意领域的最高权威身上。

senses.title: The holder of an archbishopric as an office
senses.definition: the office or dignity attached to being an archbishop, as in succeeding to the archbishopric
senses.definitionCN: 指担任大主教这一职位或尊位，如继承大主教之职
senses.example: After the old prelate died, the young bishop succeeded to the archbishop.
senses.exampleCN: 老主教去世后，年轻的主教继任了大主教之位。
senses.why: In old usage the title can stand for the office itself, metonymy of person for position.
senses.whyCN: 旧式用法中头衔可代指职位本身，属于以人代位的转喻。

intro.en: Archbishop is a compound of the Greek-derived prefix archi- and bishop, a word of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: archbishop 由希腊语来源的前缀 archi- 与日耳曼语来源的 bishop 复合而成。

items.en: Greek arkh- (ἀρχι-) meant chief or leading, attached to titles such as arkhiereus (high priest).
items.cn: 希腊语词干 arkh-（ἀρχι-）意为「首要的」，见于 arkhiereus（大祭司）等头衔。

items.en: Bishop comes from Latin episcopus, itself from Greek episkopos (overseer), borrowed into Old English as biscop.
items.cn: bishop 源自拉丁语 episcopus，再上溯希腊语 episkopos（监督者），古英语作 biscop。

items.en: The compound arcebisceop is attested in Old English, translating Latin archiepiscopus.
items.cn: 古英语已有复合词 arcebisceop，对译拉丁语 archiepiscopus。

items.en: Latin archiepiscopus combined archi- with episcopus to name the chief bishop of a province.
items.cn: 拉丁语 archiepiscopus 以 archi- 加 episcopus 指一省之首的主教。

items.en: The modern spelling archbishop was settled in Middle English after Norman French influence.
items.cn: 受诺曼法语影响，近代拼写 archbishop 在中古英语时期定型。

items.en: Today archbishop names the highest order of bishop in Anglican, Roman Catholic and Orthodox churches.
items.cn: 现代英语中 archbishop 指圣公会、天主教与东正教会中最高一级的主教。

note.en: Watch the arch- prefix: it marks chief ranks and structures, not the shape of an arch.
note.cn: 注意前缀 arch-：它标记「首要」等级或结构，与「拱形」的 arch 无关。

entries.definition: a senior clergyman in charge of a diocese
entries.definitionCN: 主管一个教区的高级神职人员，是 archbishop 的基础词

entries.definition: an angel of the highest rank
entries.definitionCN: 最高级别的天使，同样用 archi- 表示「首要」

entries.definition: a prince of the former ruling house of Austria
entries.definitionCN: （旧时奥地利皇室的）大公，archi- 表「高于」

entries.definition: a curved structure spanning an opening
entries.definitionCN: 拱形结构，只是拼写相近，词源与 arch-（首要）不同

entries.definition: in some churches, a bishop with authority over a province, equivalent to an archbishop
entries.definitionCN: 某些教会中对一省拥有主权的首席主教，与 archbishop 相当

entries.definition: the highest-ranking bishop of a country or region
entries.definitionCN: 一国或一地区的首席主教，与大主教地位相近

entries.definition: in Eastern churches, a bishop of the very highest rank
entries.definitionCN: 东正教会中的最高级主教，地位高于或相当于大主教

normalIntro.en: Use the archi- prefix and the base word bishop to fix the meaning.
normalIntro.cn: 用前缀 archi- 与基础词 bishop 锁定词义。

normal.en: archi- means chief: archi + bishop = chief bishop.
normal.cn: archi- 表「首要」：archi + bishop 即「主教之首」。

normal.en: Compare archangel (chief angel) — same prefix, same logic.
normal.cn: 对比 archangel（天使长）——同一前缀、同一逻辑。

normal.en: The Archbishop of Canterbury is the most famous example in English history.
normal.cn: 坎特伯雷大主教是英国历史上最著名的例子。

normal.en: archbishopric adds -ric (domain) for the office or district.
normal.cn: 加 -ric（辖区）构成 archbishopric，指职位或教区。

normal.en: In church hierarchy: priest < bishop < archbishop.
normal.cn: 教会等级：司铎 < 主教 < 大主教。

abstract.en: Picture a tall red-robed figure standing above a row of bishops on a cathedral staircase.
abstract.cn: 想象大教堂台阶上，一位穿红色法衣的高大身影立于众主教之上。

abstract.en: Feel the weight of a crown held high — only the chief bishop crowns a king.
abstract.cn: 感受高举王冠的分量——只有大主教能为国王加冕。

abstract.en: See the arch of a cathedral door framing the chief shepherd of the province.
abstract.cn: 想象大教堂拱门框住一省的「首席牧者」。

examples.en: The archbishop preached a sermon on forgiveness at Easter.
examples.cn: 大主教在复活节布讲了关于宽恕的布道。

examples.en: An archbishop oversees several bishops and their dioceses.
examples.cn: 大主教统辖数位主教及其教区。

examples.en: Critics dubbed her the archbishop of contemporary poetry.
examples.cn: 评论家们称她为当代诗歌的最高权威。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿奇·比帅普」——阿奇是众主教（bishop）里最威风、看起来最帅的首领，所以他是大主教。

root: 希腊语 arkh-（ἀρχι-，首要的）+ 拉丁语 episcopus / 希腊语 episkopos（监督者 → 主教）；arch- 前缀义为「首席」。

sensesIntro.en: From the literal chief bishop to metaphorical supreme authority and the office itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 由字面的「首席主教」延伸到比喻的最高权威与职位本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the chief shepherd standing above all other bishops
core.cn: 核心意象：立于众主教之上的首席牧者

branches.en: chief rank in the church
branches.cn: 教会中的首席品级

branches.en: hierarchy and the office it confers
branches.cn: 等级制及其对应的职位

branches.en: authority extended beyond the church
branches.cn: 权威延伸至教会之外

branches.en: consecration into the highest order
branches.cn: 祝圣至最高品级

branches.en: supremacy as an institutional dignity
branches.cn: 作为制度尊位的至高地位

intro.en: The archi- prefix builds titles of supreme rank across religion and nobility.
intro.cn: 前缀 archi- 构成宗教与贵族中表示至高品级的头衔。

latinIntro.en: The same Greek element passed into Latin and then the European title vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 同一希腊语成分经拉丁语进入欧洲头衔词汇。

items.meaning: an angel of the highest rank
items.example: Michael is named as an archangel.

items.meaning: a prince of the Austrian imperial house
the original model of a kind
a diocesan clergyman of high rank

definition_zh: 紫外线的；紫外区的；紫外线辐射（不可数）
definition_en: relating to the band of radiation just beyond the violet end of the visible spectrum, with shorter waves and higher energy
core_image: 石英灯发出看不见的短波光，培养皿里的菌落几分钟后全部失活
scene: 实验台上石英灯发出看不见的短波光，几分钟后培养皿里的菌落全部失活。 A quartz lamp emits ultraviolet strong enough to kill bacteria on the bench.
sceneCN: 这里 ultraviolet 指「波长比紫光更短、肉眼看不见的那段辐射」（第 1 个义项：位于可见光谱紫端之外的高能短波辐射）；句意为石英灯发出的紫外线强到能杀死台面上的细菌。可辨识物件：石英灯、培养皿、菌落、护目镜。

pos.zh: 紫外线；紫外辐射（不可数）

forms.label: 名词（紫外线；紫外辐射，不可数）

senses.title: The band beyond violet
senses.titleCN: 紫光之外的那段不可见辐射
senses.definition: the region of the electromagnetic spectrum with wavelengths shorter than visible violet but longer than X-rays
senses.definitionCN: 电磁波谱中波长比可见紫光更短、比 X 射线更长的区域
senses.example: A quartz lamp emits ultraviolet strong enough to kill bacteria on the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 石英灯发出的紫外线强到能杀死台面上的细菌。
senses.why: ultra- means beyond, so the name places this band past violet on the ordered scale of colours.
senses.whyCN: ultra- 意为「超出」，因此这个名字把这一段放在颜色次序中紫之外。

senses.title: Sunlight ultraviolet
senses.definition: the short-wave component of sunlight that reaches the ground after the atmosphere filters much of it
senses.definitionCN: 阳光中被大气滤去大半后仍到达地面的短波成分
senses.example: Sunlight ultraviolet darkens the pigment in skin.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光中的紫外线使皮肤中的色素变深。
senses.why: the sun is the everyday source, so the band is usually met as a component of daylight rather than as a lamp.
senses.whyCN: 太阳是最日常的来源，因此这一段通常作为日光的一部分被遇见，而不是作为灯。

senses.title: Sterilising ultraviolet
senses.titleCN: 用于杀菌消毒的紫外线
senses.definition: the use of short-wave ultraviolet to damage the genetic material of microbes and stop them reproducing
senses.definitionCN: 用短波紫外破坏微生物遗传物质、使其无法繁殖
senses.example: Ultraviolet treatment cleared the water of bacteria within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外线处理几分钟内就清除了水中的细菌。
senses.why: the same short waves that damage skin also damage microbial DNA, so the band becomes a tool.
senses.whyCN: 伤害皮肤的短波同样会损伤微生物的遗传物质，于是这一段成了工具。

senses.title: Ultraviolet astronomy
senses.titleCN: 紫外天文学：观测高温天体
senses.definition: the observation of hot stars and gas through their ultraviolet emission, which the atmosphere blocks from the ground
senses.definitionCN: 借高温恒星与气体的紫外辐射进行观测，而大气在地面挡住了这些辐射
senses.example: Ultraviolet astronomy must be done from orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外天文学必须从轨道上进行。
senses.why: only very hot objects emit strongly in this band, and the atmosphere absorbs it, so the technique needs space.
senses.whyCN: 只有非常高温的物体在这一段强烈辐射，而大气又吸收它，因此这项技术需要太空。

senses.title: The ultraviolet index
senses.titleCN: 紫外线指数：衡量到达地面的强度
senses.definition: a scale reporting the intensity of burning ultraviolet at the surface on a given day
senses.definitionCN: 报告某日地表灼伤性紫外线强度的指数
senses.example: The ultraviolet index reached eleven at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时紫外线指数达到十一。
senses.why: a public warning needs a number, and the number is reported under the band name.
senses.whyCN: 公共警示需要一个数字，而这个数字就以该波段的名字发布。

senses.title: Ultraviolet absorbance
senses.titleCN: 紫外吸光度：光谱分析中的读数
senses.definition: the amount of ultraviolet a sample absorbs, used to infer concentration or electronic structure
senses.definitionCN: 样品所吸收的紫外量，用来推断浓度或电子结构
senses.example: The ultraviolet absorbance told them how much protein the solution held.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外吸光度让他们知道溶液中有多少蛋白质。
senses.why: many molecules absorb specific ultraviolet wavelengths, so a single reading can measure what is present.
senses.whyCN: 许多分子会吸收特定的紫外波长，因此一次读数就能测出存在的东西。

senses.title: Ultraviolet curing
senses.titleCN: 紫外固化：用紫外光使涂层硬化
senses.definition: the curing of inks, resins or adhesives by ultraviolet light that triggers a chemical reaction
senses.definitionCN: 用紫外光触发化学反应，使油墨、树脂或胶黏剂硬化
senses.example: Ultraviolet curing sets the printing ink in under a second.
senses.exampleCN: 紫外固化在不到一秒内就让印刷油墨定形。
senses.why: the high energy of the band starts reactions that heat alone would take far longer to start.
senses.whyCN: 这一段的高能量能启动单靠加热要慢得多的反应。

senses.title: Abstract: an invisible part of a range
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：一个范围中看不见却起作用的部分
senses.definition: the portion of any range that lies past its obvious limit and still has effects, though it cannot be seen directly
senses.definitionCN: 任何范围中超出明显边界、虽不能直接看见却仍起作用的那部分
senses.example: The costs were the ultraviolet of the budget, invisible but damaging.
senses.exampleCN: 这些成本是预算中看不见的紫外部分，无形却有伤害。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the position beyond the visible edge, where effect outruns sight.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留「在可见边缘之外」这个位置：效果超出视觉所能及。

intro.en: Ultraviolet is a Latin-English hybrid: ultra, beyond, plus the English colour word violet. It dates from the 1840s, after chemical effects beyond violet were found.
intro.cn: ultraviolet 是拉丁与英语的混合词：拉丁 ultra「超出」加英语颜色词 violet。它出现于 1840 年代，在紫光之外的化学效应被发现之后。

items.en: Ultra meant beyond or on the far side, and English uses it as the prefix ultra-, as in ultrasonic and ultramarine.
items.cn: ultra 意为「超出、在远侧」，英语以 ultra- 作前缀，如 ultrasonic 与 ultramarine。

items.en: Violet goes back through Old French to Latin viola, the violet flower; the colour name is older than the physics.
items.cn: violet 经古法语上溯到拉丁 viola「堇菜」；颜色名比物理学用法更早。

items.en: Ritter found that silver salts darkened fastest beyond the violet end of a prism spectrum, showing a chemical effect where nothing was visible.
items.cn: 里特尔发现银盐在棱镜光谱紫端之外变黑最快，说明在看不见之处仍有化学作用。

items.en: The English adjective ultraviolet was formed in the 1840s, once the invisible band needed a name of its own.
items.cn: 英语形容词 ultraviolet 于 1840 年代成形，因为这段不可见波段需要一个自己的名字。

items.en: Sterilisation, the ozone layer, the ultraviolet index and curing all became familiar in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 杀菌、臭氧层、紫外线指数与固化都在 20 世纪变得常见。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact first use of ultraviolet is not agreed; ultra and viola are well attested Latin words, so no root uncertainty attaches to either half.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：ultraviolet 的确切首用无定论；ultra 与 viola 都是有据的拉丁词，因此两半都不存在词根存疑。

note.en: Group one holds the boundary words that look alike because they share ultra-; group two holds the neighbouring bands and the effects people confuse with them.
note.cn: 第一组是因共享 ultra- 而形近的边界词；第二组是相邻波段以及人们容易混淆的效应。

entries.definition: Infra- means below, so infrared lies past the red end with longer waves and lower energy.
entries.definitionCN: infra- 意为「在下」，因此红外在红端之外，波长更长、能量更低。

entries.definition: Ultra- plus marine: a deep blue pigment once shipped from beyond the sea, with nothing to do with radiation.
entries.definitionCN: ultra- 加「海」：一种曾从海外运来的深蓝颜料，与辐射无关。

entries.definition: Ultra- plus sound: vibrations above hearing, used in scanning and cleaning.
entries.definitionCN: ultra- 加「声」：高于听觉的振动，用于扫描与清洗。

entries.definition: An instrument that reveals particles too small for an ordinary microscope by scattering light sideways.
entries.definitionCN: 靠侧向散射光显示普通显微镜看不见的微粒的仪器。

entries.definition: The last visible colour before the band begins; it is the boundary ultraviolet is named against.
entries.definitionCN: 该波段开始前最后一个可见颜色；紫外线正是以它为界命名。

entries.definition: Radiation energetic enough to strip electrons from atoms; short ultraviolet belongs to this class.
entries.definitionCN: 能量足以把电子从原子中剥离的辐射；短波紫外属于这一类。

entries.definition: The band beyond ultraviolet, with even shorter waves and enough energy to pass through tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 紫外之外的那一段，波长更短，能量足以穿过组织。

entries.definition: The whole solar spectrum at the surface, of which ultraviolet is the part that burns.
entries.definitionCN: 地表的整个太阳光谱，其中造成灼伤的那部分就是紫外。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin prefix, the real experiment and the real public uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀、真实的实验与真实的公共用途。

normal.en: ultra- means beyond, so ultraviolet is the band beyond violet.
normal.cn: ultra- 意为「超出」，因此紫外是紫之外的那一段。

normal.en: Violet comes from Latin viola, the flower, so the colour name came first.
normal.cn: 紫色一词出自拉丁 viola「堇菜」，所以颜色名先于物理术语。

normal.en: The abbreviation UV is standard in labels and forecasts.
normal.cn: 两个字母的缩写在标签与预报中是标准写法。

normal.en: It both burns and sterilises, because short waves damage genetic material.
normal.cn: 它既灼伤也能杀菌，因为短波会损伤遗传物质。

normal.en: Near ultraviolet and far ultraviolet are the two subdivisions.
normal.cn: 近紫外与远紫外是两个分区。

abstract.en: Picture a room lit by a lamp everyone insists is off.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，人人都说灯关了，屋里却仍亮着。

abstract.en: Picture a colour that only the skin can read.
abstract.cn: 想象一种只有皮肤读得懂的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a cost that never appears on any invoice but still arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔从不出现在任何账单上、却仍然到来的成本。

examples.en: The ozone layer absorbs most ultraviolet before it reaches the ground.
examples.cn: 臭氧层在紫外线到达地面之前吸收了其中大部分。

examples.en: Ultraviolet lamps sterilise the air inside the hospital ward.
examples.cn: 紫外灯对病房内的空气进行杀菌。

examples.en: The forecast put the ultraviolet index at eight, high enough to burn in minutes.
examples.cn: 预报的紫外线指数为八，足以在几分钟内晒伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ultra（超出）+ violet（紫）」——排在紫色之外的那一段 → 紫外线

root: 拉丁 ultra「超出」+ 英语 violet（经古法语上溯拉丁 viola「堇菜」）；两半均为有据来源，无重构词根。英语 ultraviolet。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin at the band, then move to sunlight, sterilising, astronomy, the public index, absorbance, curing and finally the unseen part of any range.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从波段本身开始，随后走向阳光、杀菌、天文、公共指数、吸光度、固化，最后落在任何范围中看不见的那一部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp that shows nothing yet empties a dish of living colonies.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏看不见光的灯，却让一皿活菌落全部失活。

branches.en: POSITION: the prefix fixes the address past violet, and everything else follows from that place.
branches.cn: 位置：前缀把地址定在紫之外，其余义项都从这个位置而来。

branches.en: DAYLIGHT AND WARNING: the sun supplies it, and a number warns how much arrives.
branches.cn: 日光与警示：太阳提供它，一个数字警告来了多少。

branches.en: CONTROL: the same energy kills microbes and hardens resins.
branches.cn: 控制：同一份能量既能杀死微生物，也能使树脂硬化。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: hot stars and absorbing molecules are both read through this band.
branches.cn: 测量：高温恒星与吸收分子都通过这一段被读取。

branches.en: METAPHOR: whatever lies past the visible edge but still acts.
branches.cn: 比喻：位于可见边缘之外却仍然起作用的一切。

intro.en: Ultraviolet is a Latin prefix on a colour word of Latin descent, so both halves have a traceable history.
intro.cn: ultraviolet 是拉丁前缀加一个源自拉丁的颜色词，两半都有可追溯的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin ultra means beyond; Latin viola gives violet through French. The modern compound itself is nineteenth-century English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ultra 意为「超出」；拉丁 viola 经法语给出 violet。这个近代复合词本身是十九世纪英语的产物。

items.example: The prefix places the band beyond violet.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把该波段放在紫之外。

items.structure: violet (English colour word, from Old French violette, from Latin viola)
items.example: Violet is the boundary of the visible band.
items.exampleCN: 紫色是可见波段的边界。

items.meaning: the part closest to visible violet
items.meaningCN: 最靠近可见紫光的那部分
items.example: Near-ultraviolet light is used in some detectors.
items.exampleCN: 近紫外光用于某些探测器。

items.example: Far-ultraviolet light is absorbed high in the atmosphere.
items.exampleCN: 远紫外光在大气高层被吸收。

items.meaning: a lamp made to emit ultraviolet
items.example: The ultraviolet lamp sterilised the bench.
items.exampleCN: 紫外灯对台面做了杀菌。

items.meaning: a public scale of ultraviolet intensity
items.meaningCN: 紫外线强度的公共指数
items.example: The ultraviolet index warned of strong sun.
items.exampleCN: 紫外线指数提示阳光很强。
紫外光谱法测出了蛋白质。

items.meaning: how much ultraviolet a sample takes in
items.example: The ultraviolet absorbance rose with concentration.
items.exampleCN: 紫外吸光度随浓度升高。

definition_zh: 即兴的；即席的；临时的
definition_en: done or said without preparation, on the spur of the moment
core_image: 一个人被推上台，手里没有稿子，只把口袋里的笔往桌上一放就开口
scene: 主持人临时请他讲两句，他站起来就说了五分钟。 The impromptu toast turned out better than the planned one.
sceneCN: 这里 impromptu 指即席的（第 1 个义项：未经准备的发言）；句意为这段即兴祝酒比准备好的那段更好。

senses.title: Speech without preparation
senses.definition: words spoken to an audience without notes or rehearsal
senses.definitionCN: 没有稿子或排练就对听众说的话
senses.example: The impromptu toast turned out better than the planned one.
senses.exampleCN: 这段即兴祝酒比准备好的那段更好。
senses.why: The word puts readiness where preparation usually sits, and the result can surprise even the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「有准备」的位置换成「随时待命」，结果连说话者自己都可能意外。

senses.title: Performance on the spot
senses.definition: music or acting made up as it is performed
senses.definitionCN: 边演边编的音乐或表演
senses.example: The pianist gave an impromptu encore that nobody had rehearsed.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家加演了一段没人排练过的即兴曲。
senses.why: Improvisation works because the performer trusts trained reflexes more than a plan.
senses.whyCN: 即兴之所以可行，是因为表演者更信任训练出来的反射，而不是计划。

senses.title: An improvised meal
senses.definition: a meal assembled from whatever happens to be at hand
senses.definitionCN: 用手边现成的东西拼成的一餐
senses.example: They made an impromptu dinner from bread, cheese and one tomato.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用面包、奶酪和一个番茄凑成了晚餐。
senses.why: This sense extends the word from speech to things, as long as the thing is made on the spot.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把词从言语扩展到物品，只要东西是当场做成的。

senses.title: An unrehearsed remark
senses.definition: a comment that escapes before it has been shaped
senses.definitionCN: 还没被修饰就说出口的评论
senses.example: His impromptu remark was the most honest thing said all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句脱口而出的话是整晚最诚实的一句。
senses.why: What is unpolished is not always worse; polish can hide the actual thought.
senses.whyCN: 未经打磨的未必更差；打磨有时会遮住真正的想法。

senses.title: An ad hoc arrangement
senses.definition: a plan put together quickly to meet an immediate need
senses.definitionCN: 为应付眼前需要而快速拼成的安排
senses.example: The impromptu schedule worked for one week and then collapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个临时日程撑了一周就崩了。
senses.why: Quick plans buy time; the question is whether the time is used to build something sturdier.
senses.whyCN: 快速的安排买来时间；问题在于这时间是否被用来造更牢的东西。

senses.title: An impromptu gathering
senses.definition: a meeting of people arranged with almost no notice
senses.definitionCN: 几乎没提前通知就聚起来的一群人
senses.example: The impromptu gathering in the hallway lasted until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 走廊里的临时聚会一直延续到午夜。
senses.why: Some of the best gatherings happen because nobody had time to plan them badly.
senses.whyCN: 有些最好的聚会之所以发生，是因为没人有时间把它计划坏。

senses.title: An improvised solution
senses.definition: a fix invented in the moment with limited materials
senses.definitionCN: 在当下用有限材料想出的解决办法
senses.example: The impromptu repair held the bridge for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 这个临场修补让桥撑了两天。
senses.why: A fix made from what is at hand reveals how much of engineering is invention.
senses.whyCN: 用手边之物做成的修补，显出工程里有多少是临场发明。

senses.title: The charm of the unprepared
senses.definition: the liveliness that comes from having no script to follow
senses.definitionCN: 没有脚本可循而带来的生气
senses.example: What the audience loved was the impromptu quality, not the content.
senses.exampleCN: 观众喜欢的是那种即兴劲儿，而不是内容。
senses.why: The word can praise as easily as it can excuse; context decides which.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既能称赞，也能当借口；语境决定是哪一种。

intro.en: Impromptu comes from Latin for in readiness, meaning a thing available at the very moment it is needed.
intro.cn: impromptu 来自拉丁语「处于准备状态」，指在需要的那一刻正好可用的东西。

items.en: In promptu meant 'in readiness, at hand', said of troops and supplies.
items.cn: in promptu 意为「在准备中、在手边」，用于军队与补给。

items.en: Promptus meant 'brought out, ready', the participle behind prompt.
items.cn: promptus 意为「被取出、准备好的」，是 prompt 的源头。

items.en: French borrowed the phrase and used it for a short piece made on the spot.
items.cn: 法语借入这个短语，用来指当场写成的短作品。

items.en: English took it in the 17c. as both adjective and noun, including a kind of piano piece.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入，既作形容词也作名词，包括一种钢琴曲。

items.en: Modern English applies it to speeches, meals, visits and anything made without preparation.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于发言、餐食、造访，以及任何未经准备而做成的事。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the prompt root; the near-meaning group names kinds of unprepared action.
note.cn: 形近组共享 prompt 词根；近义组列出未准备行为的不同种类。

entries.definition: quick and without delay.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而不拖延的。

entries.definition: at once, without waiting.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻、不等待地。

entries.definition: the quality of being quick.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速的性质。

entries.definition: readiness and speed of action.
entries.definitionCN: 行动的敏捷与果断。

entries.definition: arising from one's own impulse, not outside pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 出于自身冲动而非外部压力的。

entries.definition: not prepared or practised beforehand.
entries.definitionCN: 事先未准备或排练的。

entries.definition: arranged for one particular purpose only.
entries.definitionCN: 仅为某一特定目的而安排的。

entries.definition: said without preparation or care.
entries.definitionCN: 未经准备或不经心说出的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a speaker standing up with empty hands and a full mind.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一个人两手空空、脑子满满地站起来」的画面。

normal.en: Impromptu hides prompt: readiness is the whole trick.
normal.cn: impromptu 里藏着 prompt：有准备状态就是全部诀窍。

normal.en: The word has no -ed and no -ly; it works as adjective, adverb and noun alike.
normal.cn: 这个词没有 -ed 也没有 -ly；它可作形容词、副词与名词。

normal.en: Think of a jazz pianist who never looks at the sheet.
normal.cn: 想象一位从不看谱的爵士钢琴家。

normal.en: Say im-PROMP-too; the stressed syllable is the moment of deciding.
normal.cn: 读成 im-PROMP-too，重读音节就是决定的那一瞬。

normal.en: Link with prompt: something prompt is ready, and impromptu is ready without prior work.
normal.cn: 和 prompt 联系：prompt 是准备好的，impromptu 是没提前准备却随时可用。

abstract.en: Preparation and improvisation are not opposites; training is what makes improvisation possible.
abstract.cn: 准备与即兴并不相反；训练才让即兴成为可能。

abstract.en: What is made on the spot carries the risk and the life of that spot.
abstract.cn: 当场做成的东西，带着那个现场的风险与生气。

abstract.en: A good improviser has practised enough to forget the practice.
abstract.cn: 好的即兴者练得足够多，才能忘掉练习。

examples.en: The impromptu toast turned out better than the planned one.
examples.cn: 这段即兴祝酒比准备好的那段更好。

examples.en: The pianist gave an impromptu encore that nobody had rehearsed.
examples.cn: 钢琴家加演了一段没人排练过的即兴曲。

examples.en: They made an impromptu dinner from bread, cheese and one tomato.
examples.cn: 他们用面包、奶酪和一个番茄凑成了晚餐。

dict_mnemonic.text: im（在）+ prompt（准备好的）+ u：处在随时可用的状态，就是「即兴」。

root: 拉丁语 in promptu（在手边、已备好），源自 promptus（准备好的）

sensesIntro.en: Impromptu always means made at the moment of use; the senses differ only in what is made, words, music, meals or gatherings.
sensesIntro.cn: impromptu 始终指在使用那一刻做成；各义项的差别只在做成了什么，言语、音乐、餐食还是聚会。

core.en: MADE AT THE MOMENT OF USE
core.cn: 在使用那一刻做成

branches.en: Words that come out already formed.
branches.cn: 一出口就已成形的话。

branches.en: Music and performance invented while played.
branches.cn: 边演边编的音乐与表演。

branches.en: Meals, gatherings and fixes assembled from what is at hand.
branches.cn: 用手边之物拼成的餐食、聚会与修补。

branches.en: Plans made quickly for immediate needs.
branches.cn: 为眼前需要快速作出的安排。

branches.en: The liveliness that comes from having no script.
branches.cn: 没有脚本带来的生气。

intro.en: The prompt family is about readiness: prompt is ready, promptly is at once, and impromptu is ready without preparation.
intro.cn: prompt 词族与准备状态有关：prompt 是准备好的，promptly 是立刻，impromptu 是没准备也随时可用。

latinIntro.en: Latin promptus means brought out and ready; the phrase in promptu places that readiness at hand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 promptus 意为被取出、已备好；短语 in promptu 把这种准备放在手边。

items.exampleCN: 她迅速的回答让我们意外。

items.example: The promptness of the staff helped.

items.meaning: the copy used to cue a play
items.example: The prompt book was full of notes.

definition_zh: 超越；超出；胜过；凌驾于……之上
definition_en: to go beyond a limit, level or ordinary range, and in older use to surpass or excel
core_image: 山路上雾线横在脚下，一个人继续往上走，穿过云层，回头已看不见那条界线
scene: 山路上雾线横在脚下，一个人继续往上走，穿过云层，回头已看不见那条界线。 Music can transcend the barrier between two languages.
sceneCN: 这里指越过某种界限（第 1 个义项：超出界限与范围）；句意为音乐能够超越两种语言之间的障碍。

pos.zh: 超越；超出；胜过；凌驾于……之上

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示状态的名词尾构成，义为「超越；超然」
由该动词的现在分词词干转成的形容词，义为「卓越的；超越的」
由前一词加表示关系的形容词尾构成，义为「先验的；超越经验的」
由形容词加表示方式的副词尾构成，义为「卓越地；超越地」

senses.title: Go beyond a limit or boundary
senses.definition: to pass across the edge of what is allowed, mapped or expected
senses.definitionCN: 越过被允许、被标定或被预期的边缘
senses.example: The path seemed to transcend the boundary of the map.
senses.exampleCN: 那条小路似乎越过了地图上的边界。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to climb over, and the oldest image is a body moving past a line rather than a number beating another number.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「爬过」，最古老的意象是身体越过一条线，而不是数字胜过另一个数字。

senses.title: Rise above the material world
senses.definition: in religion and philosophy, to move beyond bodily and worldly concerns
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教与哲学中指超出身体与世俗的关切
senses.example: Monks sought to transcend the material world.
senses.exampleCN: 僧侣们寻求超越物质世界。
senses.why: A climber who leaves the ground behind is the natural picture for a soul said to leave the world behind.
senses.whyCN: 把地面留在身后的攀登者，正是用来形容灵魂把世界留在身后的自然图像。

senses.title: Surpass others in quality
senses.definition: to be so much better than rivals that comparison no longer applies
senses.definitionCN: 比对手好得多，以致比较已不适用
senses.example: Her later work transcends every rival in the same field.
senses.exampleCN: 她后期的作品超越了同领域的每一位对手。
senses.why: Here the word is close to surpass, but it claims a different level rather than a higher score.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词接近「胜过」，但它主张的是不同的层次，而不是更高的分数。

senses.title: Outlast the age that produced it
senses.definition: of an idea or work, to remain valuable beyond the period in which it was made
senses.definitionCN: 指思想或作品在产生它的时期之后仍然有价值
senses.example: Some ideas transcend the age that produced them.
senses.exampleCN: 有些思想超越了产生它们的时代。
senses.why: Time is a boundary like any other, and what crosses it survives the terms it was born in.
senses.whyCN: 时间也是一条界线，越过它的东西便活过了自己诞生时的那些条件。

senses.title: Cross the barrier between languages or cultures
senses.titleCN: 跨越语言或文化的障碍
senses.definition: of art or feeling, to reach people who do not share a tongue or a tradition
senses.definitionCN: 指艺术或情感抵达语言或传统不同的人
senses.example: Music can transcend the barrier between two languages.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐能够超越两种语言之间的障碍。
senses.why: A barrier is a wall, and the word keeps the climbing image when it says the wall was crossed.
senses.whyCN: 障碍是一道墙，而这个词在说「墙被越过」时，保留的仍是攀爬的意象。

senses.title: Go beyond one's own limits
senses.definition: of a person, to act beyond fear, habit or the role usually played
senses.definitionCN: 指人做出超出恐惧、习惯或通常角色的行为
senses.example: He tried to transcend his own fears.
senses.exampleCN: 他试图超越自己的恐惧。
senses.why: The self can be a boundary too, and the climber may be climbing out of a former self.
senses.whyCN: 自我也可以是一条界线，攀登者也许正在爬出旧的自己。

senses.title: Lie beyond possible experience
senses.definition: in philosophy, of a question or principle that cannot be tested by experience
senses.definitionCN: 哲学上指无法由经验检验的问题或原则
senses.example: Philosophers asked whether reason could transcend experience.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问理性是否能超越经验。
senses.why: This is the technical sense: not better than experience, but outside the region where experience can go.
senses.whyCN: 这是术语义：不是比经验更好，而是在经验所能抵达的区域之外。

senses.title: Go beyond one's authority
senses.definition: of an order or act, to pass the legal or official power of the person who made it
senses.definitionCN: 指命令或行为越过作出者合法的或官方的权力
senses.example: The officer's order seemed to transcend his legal authority.
senses.exampleCN: 那名军官的命令似乎超越了他的法定权限。
senses.why: Authority is a line drawn by law, and crossing it uses the word in its plainest boundary sense.
senses.whyCN: 权限是法律画出的一条线，越过它就是这个词最朴素的「界线」义。

senses.title: Be above the created world
senses.definition: in theology, of the divine as separate from and higher than everything created
senses.definitionCN: 在神学中指神性独立于并高于一切受造之物
senses.example: Believers hold that the divine transcends the created world.
senses.exampleCN: 信徒认为神超越受造的世界。
senses.why: The highest use of the word places its subject not at the top of a scale but outside the scale altogether.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最高的用法，把主语放在不是刻度顶端、而是刻度之外的位置。

intro.en: Transcend comes from Latin transcendere, to climb over or go beyond, built from trans-, across, and scandere, to climb.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 transcendere「爬过、越过」，由 trans-「穿过」与 scandere「攀爬」构成。

items.en: Scandere meant to climb or ascend, and it also stands under the words for a ladder and for scanning a line of verse.
items.cn: scandere 意为攀爬、上升，它也是「梯子」与「按格律诵读诗句」等词的底层。

items.en: The compound meant to climb over or pass beyond, used of walls, hills and limits of every kind.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为爬过、越出，用于墙、山丘以及各种界限。

items.en: Medieval Latin made a noun for that which lies beyond the categories of ordinary thought.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出一个名词，指超出日常思想范畴的东西。

items.en: French carried the adjective into philosophy, where it named what is above the world rather than merely great in it.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词带进哲学，用来指高于世界者，而不只是世界之内的大者。

items.en: English took the verb in the late Middle Ages; the exact first date is uncertain, and the religious sense came before the general one.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪末取用这个动词；确切首见年代不确定，宗教义先于一般义出现。

items.en: Kant fixed the modern contrast between what experience can reach and what lies beyond it.
items.cn: 康德确立了现代意义上的对比：经验能抵达的东西，与处在它之外的东西。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like transcend; the second group names neighbouring ideas of going past a limit.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 transcend 相近；第二组是与「越过限度」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The state of being beyond ordinary limits or above the world.
entries.definitionCN: 指超出寻常限度或高于世界的状态。

entries.definition: Going beyond the ordinary range, often used of excellence.
entries.definitionCN: 指超出寻常范围的，常用于形容卓越。

entries.definition: Relating to what lies beyond possible experience.
entries.definitionCN: 指与超出可能经验之物相关的。

entries.definition: To climb or rise; it shares the climbing verb with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指攀登或上升；共享同一个攀爬动词，前缀不同。

entries.definition: To go down; the mirror image of climbing, built with a prefix meaning down.
entries.definitionCN: 指下降；攀爬的镜像，由意为「向下」的前缀构成。

entries.definition: To be greater than another in amount or degree; it stays inside the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 指在数量或程度上大于另一者；它仍停留在同一把刻度之内。

entries.definition: To go past a stated number or limit; it is neutral and often numerical.
entries.definitionCN: 指超过某个明示的数字或限度；中性，常指数值。

entries.definition: To be very good at something, often the best among a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某方面极好，常指群体中最好的。

entries.definition: To go faster or further than another, as one runner leaves another behind.
entries.definitionCN: 指比另一者更快或更远，像一名跑者把另一名甩在身后。

entries.definition: To perform better than someone else in the same task.
entries.definitionCN: 指在同一件事上做得比他人更好。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the climbing root, the across prefix and the contrast with mere surpassing.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用「攀爬」的词根、「穿过」的前缀，以及它与单纯「胜过」的对比。

normal.en: The prefix means across and the verb means climb, so the word pictures someone climbing over a wall.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「穿过」，词根意为「攀爬」，于是这个词画的是有人翻过一道墙。

normal.en: A ladder, a scale and a scan all come from the same climbing verb, because climbing is measuring step by step.
normal.cn: 梯子、音阶与逐行扫读都出自同一个攀爬动词，因为攀爬正是一级一级地量。

normal.en: The mountain fog line is the picture: below it is the ordinary route, above it the view changes.
normal.cn: 山上的雾线就是那幅图：线以下是寻常路线，线以上视野就变了。

normal.en: Transcend a boundary, not just a score; surpass a score, not a boundary.
normal.cn: 超越的是界线，不只是分数；胜过的是分数，不是界线。

normal.en: The word keeps a vertical direction even when the barrier is invisible, as with language or culture.
normal.cn: 即使障碍看不见，比如语言或文化，这个词仍保留着竖直的方向。

abstract.en: To transcend is to change the frame, not to win inside the old one.
abstract.cn: 超越是换掉框架，而不是在旧框架里取胜。

abstract.en: Every boundary is drawn by someone; crossing it exposes who drew it.
abstract.cn: 每条界线都由某人画出；越过它就暴露出是谁画的。

abstract.en: The word promises a higher place, and it quietly asks what ground you are leaving.
abstract.cn: 这个词许诺一个更高的位置，也悄悄追问你正把什么地面留在身后。

examples.en: The novel transcends the genre it was written in.
examples.cn: 这部小说超越了它所属的文类。

examples.en: Great architecture can transcend time and fashion.
examples.cn: 伟大的建筑能够超越时间与风尚。

examples.en: No emergency order may transcend the constitution.
examples.cn: 任何紧急命令都不得超越宪法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「传森德」——「传」过一片「森」林，到「德」国那头，已经越过界线：超越

root: 拉丁语 scandere「攀爬」→ trans-「穿过」+ scandere 构成 transcendere「爬过、越过」→ 英语 transcend「超越」；由翻墙的具体动作，扩展为越过时代、语言、经验与权限等抽象界线。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses climb from a line on a map to the top of a scale and beyond it: limits, the material world, rivals, an age, language, the self, experience, authority and the divine.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从地图上的一条线一路爬到刻度的顶端之外：界线、物质世界、对手、时代、语言、自我、经验、权限与神性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker rising through cloud until the boundary line below can no longer be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：行走者穿过云层上升，直到脚下的界线再也看不见。

branches.en: THE LIMIT BRANCH: a path crosses the edge of the map, and an order crosses the edge of lawful power.
branches.cn: 界线分支：小路越过地图边缘，命令越过合法权力的边缘。

branches.en: THE ABOVE-THE-WORLD BRANCH: a monk leaves the material world, and the divine is said to be above all created things.
branches.cn: 高于世界分支：僧侣离开物质世界，神性被说成高于一切受造之物。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON AND TIME BRANCH: a work outclasses its rivals and outlives its age.
branches.cn: 比较与时间分支：作品胜过对手，也活过自己的时代。

branches.en: THE HUMAN BARRIER BRANCH: music crosses languages and a person crosses his own fear.
branches.cn: 人的障碍分支：音乐越过语言，人越过自己的恐惧。

branches.en: THE EXPERIENCE BRANCH: a philosophical question lies outside what any test can reach.
branches.cn: 经验分支：哲学问题处在任何检验都到不了的地方。

intro.en: Transcend is a Latin compound of across and climb, and its noun and adjective family grew inside philosophy.
intro.cn: 这是一个由「穿过」与「攀爬」构成的拉丁复合词，其名词与形容词家族在哲学里长大。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the prefix trans-, the verb scandere and the compound transcendere, plus a medieval noun in -entia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供前缀 trans-、动词 scandere 与复合词 transcendere，以及一个带名词词尾的中世纪名词。

items.example: It gives the climbing a direction across a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 它给攀爬加上一条越过界线的方向。

items.example: The verb supplies the vertical picture under every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供每个义项底下的竖直图像。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms the adjective for what goes beyond.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「越出者」的形容词。

items.example: It forms the noun for the state of being beyond.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「处于之外」状态的名词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into the philosophical term.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成哲学术语。

items.structure: Latin and Greek -ismus, English noun suffix
items.example: It forms transcendentalism, the doctrine of the transcendental.

items.structure: Latin -ista, English noun suffix for a person
items.example: It forms transcendentalist, a follower of that doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transcendentalist，即信奉该学说的人。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示状态的名词尾构成，义为「超越；超然」
由该动词的现在分词词干转成的形容词，义为「卓越的；超越的」
由前一词加表示关系的形容词尾构成，义为「先验的；超越经验的」
由形容词加表示方式的副词尾构成，义为「卓越地；超越地」

definition_zh: adj. 百年的；一百周年纪念的；n. 百年纪念
definition_en: relating to a period of one hundred years; a celebration of a hundredth anniversary
core_image: 街上横挂着一条写着一百的横幅
scene: 镇上为老桥的百岁生日办了一场百年纪念。 The town held a centennial for the old bridge hundredth birthday.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：centennial 指百年纪念；句意是镇上为老桥的百岁生日举办纪念活动。

senses.title: Lasting a hundred years
senses.definition: relating to or lasting a period of one hundred years
senses.definitionCN: 与一百年时期有关的或持续百年的
senses.example: The centennial oak still stands in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 那棵百年橡树仍立在广场上。
senses.why: Latin centum is a hundred and annus is a year.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 centum 意为一百，annus 意为年。

senses.title: A hundredth anniversary
senses.definition: a celebration of the hundredth anniversary of an event or institution
senses.definitionCN: 对某一事件或机构一百周年的庆祝
senses.example: The school marked its centennial with a concert.
senses.exampleCN: 学校以音乐会纪念建校百年。
senses.why: The adjective took on the meaning of the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词又承载了纪念活动本身的意思。

intro.en: Centennial joins Latin centum, a hundred, with annus, a year.
intro.cn: centennial 由拉丁语 centum（一百）与 annus（年）组合而成。

items.en: Centum and annus supply the two halves of the word.
items.cn: centum 与 annus 提供这个词的两半。

items.en: The word is formed to mean of a hundred years.
items.cn: 十八世纪造出，意为百年的。

items.en: Centennial names a hundredth anniversary.
items.cn: 十九世纪指一百周年纪念。

items.en: The word spreads in national anniversary use.
items.cn: 十九世纪在美国的建国纪念中流行。

items.en: Schools and firms adopt centennial for their jubilees.
items.cn: 二十世纪学校与企业用它指自身纪念。

items.en: Centennial works as both adjective and noun.
items.cn: 现代兼作形容词与名词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cent- opening; the near-meaning group ranks anniversary words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cent- 开头；近义组排列周年纪念的词。

entries.definition: A Roman officer of a hundred men.

entries.definition: A temperature scale.

entries.definition: A hundredth anniversary, chiefly British.
entries.definitionCN: 百年纪念（英式）。

entries.definition: A yearly return of a date.
entries.definitionCN: 周年纪念。

entries.definition: A two hundredth anniversary.
entries.definitionCN: 两百周年纪念。

normalIntro.en: One hundred years, then the town stops to look back.
normalIntro.cn: 一百年过去，小镇停下来回望。

normal.en: Centum means a hundred.
normal.cn: centum 意为一百。

normal.en: Annus means a year.
normal.cn: annus 意为年。

normal.en: Put them together for a hundred years.
normal.cn: 合起来就是一百年。

normal.en: A banner carries the number.
normal.cn: 横幅上写着这个数字。

normal.en: The anniversary becomes a noun.
normal.cn: 周年纪念又成了名词。

abstract.en: A century folding into one day.
abstract.cn: 一个世纪折成一天。

abstract.en: Time measured in round numbers.
abstract.cn: 用整数丈量的时间。

abstract.en: A town counting its own candles.
abstract.cn: 小镇数自己的蜡烛。

examples.en: A centennial banner hung across the street.
examples.cn: 一条百年纪念横幅横跨街道。

examples.en: They planted a centennial garden near the gate.
examples.cn: 他们在门边种了一座百年纪念园。

examples.en: The centennial drew visitors from three counties.
examples.cn: 这场百年纪念吸引来三个县的访客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森天尼尔」——森林里天天数年头，数到一百就庆祝。

root: 拉丁语 centum（百）+ annus（年）→ centennial

sensesIntro.en: The word covers both the hundred-year span and the party that marks it.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词既指百年跨度，也指标记它的庆典。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a banner strung over a street for the hundredth year
core.cn: 核心意象：为第一百个年头横跨街道的横幅

branches.en: An oak older than the road.
branches.cn: 比这条路更老的橡树。

branches.en: A ledger of a hundred harvests.
branches.cn: 记满一百次收成的账本。

branches.en: A banner with three zeroes.
branches.cn: 写着三个零的横幅。

branches.en: A hall of old photographs.
branches.cn: 摆满旧照片的大厅。

branches.en: A hundred years made visible for a day.
branches.cn: 让一百年在一天里显形。
